actions.name: create_account_contacts
actions.description: Create an association. Links a contact to an account, optionally with the contact's job title there. A contact can be linked to only one account; to move it, change or delete its existing link. Saving a link also sets the contact's account (`orgid` and `orgname` on the contact) and can start automations that run when a contact's account changes. Needs permission to edit contacts.

contact.description: ID of an existing contact that is not linked to a different account.

jobTitle.description: The contact's job title at the account.

actions.name: list_account_contacts
actions.description: List all associations. Lists links between contacts and accounts. Filter by contact to find a contact's account, or by account to list its contacts. Each link also carries the date and type of the newest of these activities with the contact: a one-to-one email, a campaign sent to them, an automation they started or finished, a forward or reply, a text sent or received, an automation goal they reached, or a deal task. Results come in no guaranteed order. For some accounts, users outside the Admin group see only links for contacts on lists they can access, or on no list.

filters[contact].description: Return only links for this contact ID.

filters[account].description: Return only links for this account ID.

limit.description: How many links to return. Defaults to 20; values over 100 return 100.

offset.description: How many links to skip. Defaults to 0.

actions.name: get_account_contact
actions.description: Retrieve an association. Returns one link between a contact and an account. No list permissions are applied.

id.description: ID of the link.

actions.name: update_account_contact
actions.description: Update an association. Changes a link. Send only the fields to change; the others keep their values. Changing `account` moves the contact to that account. Saving a link also sets the contact's account (`orgid` and `orgname` on the contact) and can start automations that run when a contact's account changes. Changing `contact` does not clear `orgid` and `orgname` on the contact that was linked before. Needs permission to edit contacts. PATCH /accountContacts/{id} does the same thing.

id.description: ID of the link.

account.description: ID of an existing account to move the contact to.

contact.description: ID of an existing contact that is not linked to a different account.

jobTitle.description: The contact's job title at the account.

actions.name: delete_account_contacts
actions.description: Delete an association. Removes a contact from an account. The contact and the account are kept. The contact's account (`orgid` and `orgname` on the contact) is cleared, which can start automations that run when a contact's account changes. Needs permission to edit contacts.

id.description: ID of the link.

actions.name: get_contact_events_and_activities
actions.description: List a contact's activity history: recent events such as campaign emails sent, link clicks, list and automation changes, notes. The activity feed of one contact: its history of what the contact has done recently and which campaigns and emails were sent to it, as events recorded over time. Email opens are not activities: this feed shows sends (Log) and clicks (LinkData) but cannot say whether the contact opened an email. Send contact with the contact id. The request first refreshes that contact's feed from the underlying tables, so recent events appear, then returns the entries. A request without contact reads activities across the whole account; on a large account that scans millions of r...

contact.description: The contact id. Always send it: without it the read covers every activity on the account. Several contacts can be read at once by repeating the key, contact[]=1&contact[]=2.

after.description: Return only entries recorded strictly after this date and time. Any common date format is accepted; a value without a timezone offset is read in the platform timezone, the one the response's other timestamps carry. An unreadable value returns 422.

type.description: Return only entries of these kinds. One or more API type names separated by commas: log, link-data, mpp-link-data, forward, reply, update, contact-email, contact-list, contact-automation, automation-block, note, contact-log, tracking-log, sms-log, sms-reply, sms-unsub, deal-activity, deal-task, contact-conversion, ecom-order-activity, hilos-flow, hilos-conversation, enrichment, omni-channel-link-data, fb-audience-contact-log, contact-restore-activity. These are the reference_type values written in lower case with dashes, with contact in place of subscriber and automation in place of series; the response's referenceModelName uses the same spelling. The reference_type spelling itself, for example Log or SubscriberList, is accepted too.

emails.description: A switch. When the parameter is present with any value, including 0, only one-to-one email activity is returned: SubscriberEmail entries, Reply entries, and deal activities that carry a connected-mailbox email. Leave it out to see every kind of activity.

include.description: Related records to attach, separated by commas. The reference record itself is always attached. Values: notes, notes.user, recipients, recipients.recipient, reference, reference.automation, reference.campaign, reference.campaign.campaignList, reference.campaign.campaignMessage, reference.campaignMessage, reference.contact, reference.contactList, reference.contactList.list, reference.deal, reference.deal.contact, reference.dealTasktype, reference.link, reference.list, reference.log, reference.log.campaign, reference.log.contact, reference.log.message, reference.message, reference.note, reference.sms, reference.sms.automation, user

orders[tstamp].description: Order entries by when they happened: asc for oldest first, desc for newest first.

limit.description: Number of entries to return per request. Defaults to 20; the maximum is 100, and asking for more is capped at 100.

offset.description: Number of entries to skip before returning results. Use with limit to page.

actions.name: get_activity_entry
actions.description: Retrieve one activity entry. Returns one entry of a contact's activity feed by its id. Use it to re-read an entry found through GET /activities. The fields are the same as in the list, except notes and recipients, which appear only in the list. The response carries the entry only: the underlying record is not attached, so read it from the endpoint for its type, using reference.type and reference.id. Unlike GET /activities, this read does not refresh the contact's feed first.

id.description: The activity entry id, the id field of a GET /activities entry.

actions.name: list_activity_recipients
actions.description: List all activity recipients. Lists the activity recipient records in the account. Each record links one entry of a contact's activity feed (see GET /activities) to the contact it is about. A record is written for each new activity entry, always with reltype Subscriber and the contact id in relid. The activity entry's own subscriberid holds the same contact. Saving a change to an entry writes another record, so one entry can have several records. A merge moves the merged contact's records to the surviving contact. The list has no filters or sort options, and records come in no guaranteed order. It does not check the linked activity, so it can return records that GET /activityRecipients/{i...

limit.description: Number of records to return. Defaults to 20; values above 100 are treated as 100.

offset.description: Number of records to skip. Use with limit to page through the records.

ids.description: Comma-separated record IDs to return. When set, only those records are returned; limit does not apply, but offset still does.

actions.name: retrieve_activity_recipient
actions.description: Retrieve an activity recipient. Returns one activity recipient record by its ID, under activityRecipient. The linked activity entry comes beside it, under activities. Returns 404 if no record has the id. Returns 403 when the linked activity entry cannot be read. That happens when the activity entry no longer exists, or it is filtered out for this caller: a deal activity when the caller has no deal access, a mailbox email in another user's private mailbox, an entry for a deal the caller does not own (without permission to see all deals), or a list subscription that was removed.

id.description: ID of the activity recipient record.

actions.name: retrieve_activity_of_activity_recipient
actions.description: Retrieve the activity of an activity recipient. Returns the activity entry this record links to, under activity, in the same shape as GET /activities/{id}. The body is an empty object {} in the cases where GET /activityRecipients/{id} returns 403: when the activity entry no longer exists, or it is filtered out for this caller: a deal activity when the caller has no deal access, a mailbox email in another user's private mailbox, an entry for a deal the caller does not own (without permission to see all deals), or a list subscription that was removed. Returns 404 if no record has the id.

id.description: ID of the activity recipient record.

actions.name: retrieve_recipient_of_activity_recipient
actions.description: Retrieve the recipient of an activity recipient. Returns the record that relid points to. The record type comes from reltype and sets the response key. Records are written with reltype Subscriber, so the response is the contact, under contact. The body is an empty object {} when the contact no longer exists or relid is 0. Users outside the Admin group also get {} when the contact is only on lists their group may not access. This read does not check the linked activity entry. Returns 404 if no record has the id.

id.description: ID of the activity recipient record.

actions.name: save_automation_from_drafted_schema
actions.description: Save an automation from a drafted schema. Persists the automation described by the schema JSON string from a prior draft call. A repeated sessionId returns the existing series. A missing sessionId, or a session with no prior build, still creates one. Answers 403 when the API user may not manage automations or when entitlements block triggers or actions in the proposal, and 500 when the builder or model fails.

labelId.description: Folder label id when the automation should be filed under a label.

Answers 403 when the API user may not manage automations, 422 when the model returns more than one workflow in one call, and 500 when the builder or model fails.

customerWords.description: The customer's original words when the brief or prompt may omit a name the automation should reuse.

name.description: Display name shown in the composer.

actions.name: check_whether_automation_can_be_edited
actions.description: Check whether an automation can be edited. Says whether one automation can be edited. Answers 200 with allow, reason, and a link to the automation. Allow is false when the automation is turned on (ACTIVE), missing (OTHER), still being updated (IN_PROGRESS), or an import still needs mapping (NEEDS_MAPPING). Answers 403 when the API user may not manage automations. sessionId, source, and currentSeriesId are accepted and logged. They do not change allow. The first check after a build with external emails completes can change the automation: it clears loading on send blocks the writer never filled, sets a segment error on conditions waiting on those emails, and sends a builder refresh.

id.description: Id of the automation to check.

source.description: Request source. Logged only. It does not change allow.

currentSeriesId.description: Series id the caller is viewing. Logged only. It does not change allow.

actions.name: edit_automation_from_prompt

A refused edit answers 409 with allow false, reason, link, and error_code EDIT_DENIED. Reason is ACTIVE when the automation is turned on, OTHER when it is missing, and NEEDS_MAPPING when an import still needs mapping. An edit or build already in progress answers 409 with error and error_code EDIT_IN_PROGRESS. Answers 403 when the API user may not manage automations, or when the account lacks entitlements for a trigger or action in the edit.

id.description: Id of the automation to edit.

prompt.description: What to change on the automation, in the customer's words.

labelId.description: Folder id to store the automation in, when the caller sends one.

failOnError.description: When true, the edit stops on the first blocking error.

sessionId.description: Automation agent session identifier when the caller is continuing a chat turn. A repeat call with the same session still runs the edit again.

source.description: Request source. Accepted and logged. It does not change whether the edit is allowed.

caller.description: Optional request origin for telemetry. Only the value `mcp` changes caller metrics on the long onboarding routes.

currentSeriesId.description: Series id the caller is viewing. Accepted and logged. It does not change whether the edit is allowed.

referencedAssets.description: Lists, tags, or other composer chips the caller attached to the prompt.

items.description: A list, tag, or other asset the automation composer attached to the prompt.

pkey.description: Primary key of the asset in its store.

asset_type.description: Asset type identifier, such as list or tag.

name.description: Display name shown in the composer.

skipCampaignGeneration.description: When true, skip LLM campaign generation for send blocks the edit adds or rewrites.

externalEmailWriter.description: When true, return send step to block pairings for an external email writer.

senderMessage.description: The sender's own message for this turn, word for word, when the caller rewrote it into `prompt`. With `externalEmailWriter`, the edit is planned and its changes to existing steps are checked against it.

earlierSenderMessages.description: The sender's own messages from earlier turns of the conversation, oldest first, word for word. Read with `sender_message` when it refers back to them.

contentEditedCampaignIds.description: Campaigns the caller already edited the content of this turn. With `externalEmailWriter`, the edit does not replace or clear the email of a step that sends one of them.

actions.name: list_brand_kits
actions.description: List all brand kits. List every brand kit on the account. Each item has the same shape as Retrieve a brand kit; the primary kit carries brandkit.isPrimary=true.

orders[created_timestamp].description: Order brand kits by creation time: ASC for oldest first, DESC for newest first. Omitted, the order is unspecified. created_timestamp is the only sortable field.

actions.name: get_primary_brand_kit
actions.description: Retrieve the default (primary) brand kit. Get the account's default brand kit, also called its primary brand kit: which kit is the default now, falling back to the most recently created one if none is marked primary. Use it to confirm the current default, including after Set the default (primary) brand kit.

includeSiteSummary.description: Include the LLM-generated site summary in the response, generating it on demand if a scraped snapshot exists but no summary has been produced yet. Never scrapes.

includeSitePages.description: Include the stored site page snapshots the summary is built from.

actions.name: get_brand_kit
actions.description: Retrieve a brand kit. Get a single brand kit by UUID.

actions.name: update_brand_kit
actions.description: Update a brand kit. Update the properties of an existing brand kit. A property left out of brandData keeps its stored value; one sent as null, an empty string or an empty list is cleared. Objects (colors, fonts, companyLocation) are merged key by key, and a list (links, logos, industries and so on) is replaced by the list sent, so send every entry to keep. Which kit is the account's primary kit is not part of that data: isPrimary is ignored if sent, and Set the default (primary) brand kit is the operation that changes it.

brandData.description: The brand kit fields a create or update request can set, in one object.

name.description: Brand/company name.
e.g. 'twitter'.

cta.description: Hex, call-to-action button background. Optional; falls back to primary.

text.description: Hex, body text on the light background. Optional.

textOnDark.description: Hex, body text on the dark background. Optional.

fonts.description: Brand fonts. Families must match the font catalogue; unrecognized values are dropped.

buttonStyle.description: Primary button shape. Optional; lengths must be px, rem, em or %, and invalid values are dropped.

spacing.description: Spacing scale. Optional; lengths must be px, rem, em or %, and invalid values are dropped.

imageStyle.description: Kind of imagery the brand uses. Optional; invalid values are dropped.

mood.description: Short mood, e.g. 'warm, candid'. Up to 80 characters.

guidance.description: Guidance for choosing or generating images. Up to 400 characters.

websiteUrl.description: Website URL of the brand. On update, leaving it out keeps the stored value. When it is sent empty, or left out on create, https:// followed by domain is stored instead.

domain.description: e.g. 'acme.com'. Derived from websiteUrl when unset.

brandkitName.description: Display name that tells same-named kits apart (language appended). Distinct from name.

competitors.description: Up to 5 competitor names or domains. On update it replaces the whole list, so to add or remove one, read the current list with Retrieve a brand kit's competitors and send the list you want; leave it out to keep the current list. Triggers async enrichment. Not returned by Retrieve a brand kit.

tone.description: Brand voice/tone. Triggers async enrichment. Not returned by Retrieve a brand kit; read it with Retrieve a brand kit's tone.

actions.name: delete_brand_kit
actions.description: Delete a brand kit. Permanently delete a brand kit together with its generated templates, preview images and brand history. Deleting the primary brand kit makes the most recently created remaining kit primary.

actions.name: get_brand_kit_history
actions.description: Retrieve a brand kit's website history. Get the latest stored snapshot of the brand's homepage as markdown and every recorded change to it, for any brand kit. When nothing has been stored yet the homepage is scraped first, so the first call takes longer. Set includeSitePages to also get the stored important pages of the website with their recent changes.

includeSitePages.description: Set to true (or 1, yes, on) to also return the stored important pages of the website and their recent changes under sitePages. Anything else, or leaving it out, returns the homepage only.

actions.name: get_brand_kit_competitors
actions.description: Retrieve a brand kit's competitors. Get the competitors of any brand kit, not only the primary one. Competitors are stored apart from the brand kit record, so Retrieve a brand kit and List all brand kits do not return them. An empty list means the kit has no competitors only when status is complete; when status is not_started, pending or failed the competitors are not available yet.

actions.name: set_primary_brand_kit
actions.description: Set the default (primary) brand kit. Make one brand kit the account's default, also called its primary brand kit: the "Set as default brand" action. The named kit becomes primary and every other brand kit on the account stops being primary. Takes no request body and changes none of the kit's own data. Update a brand kit cannot change which kit is primary. The response body is empty; read Retrieve the default (primary) brand kit to confirm the new default.

uuid.description: UUID of the brand kit to make the account's default.

body.description: The JSON ActiveCampaign takes for this call, as its API docs show it. Leave out when the call needs nothing more than its ids.

actions.name: refresh_brand_kit_tone
actions.description: Refresh a brand kit's tone. Queues a new tone extraction for the brand kit and returns without waiting for it. The stored tone is replaced when it finishes; poll Retrieve a brand kit's tone for progress. Refused while an extraction is already pending.

body.description: The JSON ActiveCampaign takes for this call, as its API docs show it. Leave out when the call needs nothing more than its ids.

actions.name: get_brand_kit_tone
actions.description: Retrieve a brand kit's tone. Get the brand voice and tone of any brand kit, not only the primary one. Tone is stored apart from the brand kit record, so Retrieve a brand kit and List all brand kits do not return it. An empty tone means the kit has none only when status is complete; when status is not_started, pending or failed the tone is not available yet.

actions.name: update_ai_instruction_of_account
actions.description: Update the AI instruction of the account. Replaces the text of the instruction the AI agent follows for every user on the account. It is 404 when the account has no instruction yet; use the create operation first. Only admin users of the account can update it.

content.description: The instruction the AI agent follows for everyone on the account. At most 4000 characters, without emoji.

actions.name: create_ai_instruction_of_account
actions.description: Create the AI instruction of the account. Saves the instruction the AI agent follows for every user on the account. An account has at most one, so this is 409 when one already exists; use the update operation to change it. Only admin users of the account can create it.

content.description: The instruction the AI agent follows for everyone on the account. At most 4000 characters, without emoji.

actions.name: delete_ai_instruction_of_account
actions.description: Delete the AI instruction of the account. Removes the instruction the AI agent follows for every user on the account. Only admin users of the account can delete it.

actions.name: list_ai_instructions_of_account
actions.description: List the AI instructions of the account. Returns the instruction the account has given the AI agent, which the agent follows for every user on the account. The instructions array is empty when the account has not set one. Any user of the account can read it.

actions.name: get_ecommerce_customer_behavior_summary
actions.description: Retrieve an ecommerce customer behavior summary. Customers with completed or recovered orders in a date window, split per connection (store) into new (one order in the window), repeat (more than one order in the window) and inactive (latest order in the window is more than 90 days before the end of the window). Inactivity is measured from endDate, not from today, and only orders inside the window are looked at, so a window of 90 days or less, including the default 30-day window, never has inactive customers. The three groups do not overlap, so they add up to that connection total_customers. Because a customer who shops at two stores is counted once for each, the grand total_customers is n...

startDate.description: First day of the window, as YYYY-MM-DD, counted from 00:00:00. Send it together with endDate or not at all. When both are omitted the window is the last 30 days.

endDate.description: Last day of the window, as YYYY-MM-DD, counted through 23:59:59. Send it together with startDate or not at all, and never before startDate. When both are omitted the window ends today.

connectionId.description: Restrict the result to one ecommerce connection (store) by its id, as listed by GET /connections. A positive integer. When omitted the result covers every connection.

behaviorType.description: Add additional_metrics for one group: repeat_customers, new_customers or inactive_customers. When omitted there is no additional_metrics.

actions.name: get_ecommerce_order_status_summary
actions.description: Retrieve an ecommerce order status summary. How many ecommerce orders are in each state in a date window, with completion and abandonment rates. Unlike the revenue summary this counts every state, abandoned and pending carts included, so its total_orders is not comparable with the revenue summary order_count. completion_rate and abandonment_rate exclude open carts from the denominator; the two _effective_percent rates include them. Rates are percentages returned as strings with two decimals.

startDate.description: First day of the window, as YYYY-MM-DD, counted from 00:00:00. Send it together with endDate or not at all. When both are omitted the window is the last 30 days.

endDate.description: Last day of the window, as YYYY-MM-DD, counted through 23:59:59. Send it together with startDate or not at all, and never before startDate. When both are omitted the window ends today.

connectionId.description: Restrict the result to one ecommerce connection (store) by its id, as listed by GET /connections. A positive integer. When omitted the result covers every connection.

actions.name: get_ranked_ecommerce_products
actions.description: Retrieve ranked ecommerce products. Products ranked by revenue, units sold or order frequency over a date window, counting only completed and recovered orders (abandoned and pending carts are excluded), aggregated across orders by the product external id within each connection, so the same product sold through two connections is two entries. Page through the ranking with limit and offset; total_products_found is the size of the whole ranking, not of the page.

startDate.description: First day of the window, as YYYY-MM-DD, counted from 00:00:00. Send it together with endDate or not at all. When both are omitted the window is the last 30 days.

endDate.description: Last day of the window, as YYYY-MM-DD, counted through 23:59:59. Send it together with startDate or not at all, and never before startDate. When both are omitted the window ends today.

connectionId.description: Restrict the result to one ecommerce connection (store) by its id, as listed by GET /connections. A positive integer. When omitted the result covers every connection.

rankBy.description: What to rank by: revenue, quantity (units sold) or frequency (number of orders containing the product). Defaults to revenue.

limit.description: Maximum products to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 10.

offset.description: Products to skip before the first returned, for paging. Defaults to 0.

actions.name: get_ecommerce_revenue_summary
actions.description: Retrieve an ecommerce revenue summary. Revenue for completed and recovered ecommerce orders in a date window: the order count and the number of distinct customers who placed them, broken down by currency and, when no connectionId is given, by connection (store). Already-formatted money strings are returned beside the raw amounts. Orders in any other state, such as abandoned or pending carts, are not counted; use the order status summary for those. A window of orders is chosen by the date the order was created in the store, not the date it reached ActiveCampaign. Counts and raw amounts are returned as numeric strings, exactly as the database reports them.

startDate.description: First day of the window, as YYYY-MM-DD, counted from 00:00:00. Send it together with endDate or not at all. When both are omitted the window is the last 30 days.

endDate.description: Last day of the window, as YYYY-MM-DD, counted through 23:59:59. Send it together with startDate or not at all, and never before startDate. When both are omitted the window ends today.

connectionId.description: Restrict the result to one ecommerce connection (store) by its id, as listed by GET /connections. A positive integer. When omitted the result covers every connection.

currency.description: Restrict the result to one currency, as a three-letter upper-case ISO 4217 code such as USD. When omitted every currency is included and reported separately.

actions.name: get_contact_trends_for_list
actions.description: Retrieve contact trends for a list. Daily contact and unsubscribe totals for a date window, the same numbers as the Contact Trends report. Pass list_id for one list. Omit it, or send 0, for every list the caller can access. A caller who is not a main-group admin only receives lists they are allowed to see. unsubscribe_total is the count of memberships still unsubscribed whose unsubscribe date falls in the window. The series is built from the current membership row, so a contact who left and later resubscribed is counted from the latest subscribe date only, and a deleted contact is absent.

list_id.description: List id. Omit it, or send 0, for every list the caller can access. The query key is list_id.

from.description: First day of the window, as YYYY-MM-DD, counted from 00:00:00. Required, and must be on or before to.

to.description: Last day of the window, as YYYY-MM-DD, counted through 23:59:59. Required, and must be on or after from.

graph.description: Which series to calculate. active_contacts and total_contacts are daily running contact totals. new_contacts is joins per day (subscribe date on one list, contact created date when list_id is omitted). unsubscribes makes unsubscribe_total the count of unsubscribes in the window. Omit it for the Contact Trends default, a daily running total that does not restrict the start count to memberships that are still active.

actions.name: list_audiences
actions.description:
List Summaries for Saved Segments. Lists the account's Saved Segments with their summary: name, category, contact counts and dates.

A Saved Segment is a segment that has a `name` (a name cannot be added after a segment is created, it must be set when the segment is created). Saved Segments are displayed on the app/segments page. A segment without a `name` is not a Saved Segment and does not have a summary.

Saved Segment summaries can be found by listing them or by searching by name with the `search` param. To read a segment's definition use `GET /api/3/segmentsV2/{segmentId}`.

The `counts` attribute contains `last_total` and `last_active_total`. These results are from the segment's las...

sort.description: Single sort value. Dash sign indicates descending order

search.description: Search for Saved Segments by name. Not case sensitive

actions.name: get_audiences
actions.description:
Retrieve a Saved Segment's Summary. Retrieves the summary (name, category, contact counts, dates) of one Saved Segment by its UUID.

Get the UUID from `GET /api/3/audiences` (list them or search by name with `search`). Contact counts are from the segment's last evaluation run, not live.

Only Saved Segments have a summary: segments that have a `name`. A segment without a `name` returns 404 here even though the segment exists. If you are not sure the segment is a Saved Segment, call `GET /api/3/segmentsV2/{segmentId}` first and check for a `name`.

To read the segment's definition use `GET /api/3/segmentsV2/{segmentId}`.

segmentId.description: The Saved Segment's UUID. Numeric (legacy) segment IDs never have a summary and return 404.

actions.name: list_automations
actions.description: List all automations.

limit.description: Number of automations to return. Defaults to 20, and values above 100 are reduced to 100.

offset.description: Number of automations to skip, for paging.

entryDateStart.description: When set together with `entryDateEnd`, return only automations that had at least one run entry between these dates (inclusive). Both parameters are required to apply the window. Day boundaries use the signed-in user's time zone. Each returned automation includes `entriesInWindow`, the count of runs in that window. `meta.entryWindowApplied` is true when the window was applied. `entered` and `exited` on each row remain all-time totals. When the windowed count cannot complete in time, the response falls back to the normal roster and `meta.entryWindowApplied` is false.

entryDateEnd.description: Inclusive end date for the entry window. Must be sent with `entryDateStart`. Format `YYYY-MM-DD`.

ids.description: Return only these automations. One id, or several separated by commas. Supersedes `limit`, which becomes the number of ids given.

search.description: Return only automations whose name contains this text.

active.description: Split automations by whether they are live. A true value (`1` or `true`) returns every automation past draft — active, inactive and paused alike. A false value (`0` or `false`) returns drafts only, not inactive or paused automations. Omit the parameter to return all of them.

has_message.description: Set to any non-empty value to return only automations that send a campaign, an SMS or a site message.

label.description: Return only automations in these folders. One folder id, or several separated by commas. `-1` means automations in no folder.

enhance.description: Set to any non-empty value to include each automation's block, goal, campaign, label and conversion data alongside the automations themselves.

statusCounts.description: Set to any non-empty value to include a count of automations per status next to the results.

show_has_goal.description: Set to any value other than `false` to mark whether each automation already has a business goal attached.

map.description: Set to any truthy value when the results are being drawn as the automations map. Once more than 100 automations match, the map cannot render them all, so the results are narrowed to the automations that reference one another through their blocks. Under 100 matches it changes nothing.

filters[name].description: Filter by the automation's name. A partial match: `renew` matches `Renewal reminder`.

filters[status].description: Filter by the automation's status: 0 draft, 1 active, 2 inactive, 3 paused. Several statuses may be given separated by commas.

filters[hidden].description: Filter by whether the automation is hidden. 1 hidden, 0 not. Defaults to 0 when the parameter is omitted, so hidden automations are left out unless they are asked for.

filters[entered].description: Filter by the total number of contacts that have entered the automation.

filters[exited].description: Filter by the total number of contacts that have left the automation.

filters[cdate].description: Filter by the automation's created date.

filters[mdate].description: Filter by the automation's last modified date.

filters[ids].description: Return only these automations. One id, or several separated by commas.

filters[tag].description: Return only automations that add or remove this tag id.

filters[triggers].description: Return only automations started by these trigger types, separated by commas.

filters[actions].description: Return only automations containing these action block types, separated by commas.

filters[label_name].description: Return only automations in the folder with this name.

orders[hidden].description: Order by whether the automation is hidden.

orders[entered].description: Order by the total number of contacts that have entered the automation.

orders[exited].description: Order by the total number of contacts that have left the automation.

orders[cdate].description: Order by the automation's created date.

orders[mdate].description: Order by the automation's last modified date.

orders[revisions].description: Order by when the automation was last revised, falling back to its last modified date when it has never been revised. Sent without a direction, this orders descending.

orders[currentContacts].description: Order by the number of contacts currently moving through the automation. Sent without a direction, this orders descending.

actions.name: bulk_edit_automations
actions.description: Bulk edit automations. Activate or deactivate every automation listed in `seriesIds` in a single call (status 1 = active, 2 = inactive). Mass mutation, not a listing.

seriesIds.description: A list of automation IDs to be made active/inactive

status.description: 1 = Activate, 2 = Inactive

reactivateAt.description: When a paused automation should become active again. Read only when status is 3 (paused) and scheduled reactivation is enabled; must be a date and time in the future and within the pause window, else 422.

actions.name: get_automation
actions.description: Retrieve an automation. Returns one automation's metadata (name, status, id). It does not include triggers, actions, or conditions. Use GET /automations with the search query parameter to find an automation by name when the id is not known, then call GET /automations/{id}/blocks for its contents. A row from GET /automations is not that automation unless its id matches the id you asked for.

id.description: ID of the automation to retrieve

actions.name: get_automation_blocks
actions.description: Retrieve an automation's blocks. Returns the trigger, actions, waits, conditions, and goals that make up one automation: each block's id, seriesid, parentid, ordernum, type, and params. This is the read for what is inside a single automation. It is not an account-wide list and not contact run history.

id.description: ID of the automation whose blocks to retrieve

actions.name: get_automation_triggers
actions.description: Retrieve an automation's start triggers. Returns the start records for one automation in `automationTriggers`: each record's id, type, and params (for example a tag-added start has type `tagadd` and the tag name in `params.tag`). Use this with retrieve-automation-blocks when the start block only lists trigger ids and the goal needs how a contact enters. This is not GET /automations/triggers (the account-wide trigger-type catalog) and not contact run history.

id.description: ID of the automation whose start triggers to retrieve

actions.name: list_automation_contacts
actions.description: List all contacts in an automation. List the contacts currently in, or that have run through, a single automation. This is a paginated equivalent of filtering `/api/3/contactAutomations` by `filters[seriesid]`.

seriesId.description: ID of the automation to receive contacts for

filters[subscriberid].description: Filter by contact ID. Supported operators: `eq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `in`. Example: `filters[subscriberid][gt]=10`

filters[status].description: Filter by run status: 1 = in progress, 2 = ended. Supported operators: `eq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `in`. Example: `filters[status][gt]=1`

filters[lastblock].description: Filter by the ID of the last automation block the contact reached. Supported operators: `eq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `in`. Example: `filters[lastblock][gt]=5`

filters[adddate].description: Filter by the date the contact entered the automation. Accepts `YYYY-MM-DD` (matches the whole day) or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. Supported operators: `eq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `in`. Example: `filters[adddate][gt]=2026-01-01`

orders[adddate].description: Order by the date the contact entered the automation

limit.description: The number of records to return per request. Defaults to 20 and is capped at 100.

offset.description: Offset index of records to return.

actions.name: get_contact_automation_steps
actions.description: Retrieve recorded steps for one contact automation run. Returns the steps recorded for one enrollment in an automation, including the skip reason saved for that contact when a step was skipped. Use the contact automation id from GET /contactAutomations or GET /contacts/{id}/contactAutomations. Returns 404 when the enrollment does not exist for that automation. An enrollment with no recorded steps returns an empty steps list; it does not explain why a contact never entered.

actions.name: list_bounce_logs
actions.description: List all bounce logs. Every bounce log entry on the account, one per bounced message with its timestamp, bounce code, contact and campaign. Filter to one contact with filters[subscriberid]. filters[tstamp] matches one exact timestamp, not a range, so there is no way to count bounces for a date range in one request; to bound by time, sort with orders[tstamp] and page until the entries pass the boundary. meta.total is the number of matching entries. Unknown filter keys are ignored rather than rejected, so the response can look filtered when it is not, and an operator on a known key such as filters[tstamp][gt] is applied as an exact match with that value, not as a range. 20 entries per reque...

filters[subscriberid].description: Return only the bounce logs of this contact id.

filters[tstamp].description: Return only bounce logs recorded at exactly this timestamp. This is an exact match, not a range.

limit.description: Number of bounce logs to return per request. Defaults to 20; the maximum is 100, and asking for more is capped at 100.

offset.description: Number of bounce logs to skip before returning results. Use with limit to page.

actions.name: list_brandings
actions.description: List all brandings. List all existing branding resources

actions.name: get_branding
actions.description: Retrieve a branding. Retrieve an existing branding resource

actions.name: update_branding
actions.description: Update a branding. Update an existing branding resource

id.description: Branding ID

groupid.description: The group ID. This value will always be 3.

siteName.description: Title of software. Example: 'ActiveCampaign Email Marketing'

siteLogoSmall.description: URL of small logo. Small logos appear in the header of the admin panel.

headerTextValue.description: Content of non-removable header. Example: text header content

headerHtmlValue.description:
Content of non-removable header. Example:

header content here

footerTextValue.description: Content of non-removable footer. Example: text footer content

footerHtmlValue.description:
Content of non-removable footer. Example:

footer content here

links.description: External links. To enable (which is the default) exclude this parameter entirely. To disable (remove our branding), just pass this parameter with any value.

adminTemplateHtm.description: The actual HTML template (ONLY AVAILABLE FOR CERTAIN PLANS)

adminTemplateCss.description: The actual CSS. Example: test color: green; (ONLY AVAILABLE FOR CERTAIN PLANS)

publicTemplateHtm.description: The actual HTML template (ONLY AVAILABLE FOR CERTAIN PLANS)

publicTemplateCss.description: The actual CSS. Example: test color: green; (ONLY AVAILABLE FOR CERTAIN PLANS)

actions.name: list_business_goal_data
actions.description: List business goals (agent-oriented read). A read-optimized listing of business goals, separate from GET /initiatives/{initiativeId}. Returned directly from InitiativeAgentDataService::getInitiatives(). Conversions are always included inline for every business goal; conversion trigger detail (conversionEvents) is only populated on the single-goal endpoint, never here. Assets (automations, campaigns, forms, sms) are included inline only when includeAssets=true -- otherwise every assets list comes back empty.

limit.description: Number of business goals per page, 1 to 100.

isArchived.description: 1 to list archived business goals, 0 to list active ones.

search.description: Only business goals whose name contains this text.

includeAssociationCounts.description: Accepted by the underlying query DTO shared with GET /initiatives, but currently has no effect on this endpoint: InitiativeAgentDataController::getInitiatives() never reads GetInitiativesQuery::getShouldIncludeAssociationCounts(), and InitiativeAgentDataService::getInitiatives() has no parameter for it. The response never carries association counts regardless of this value.

includeConversionLabels.description: Accepted by the underlying query DTO shared with GET /initiatives, but currently has no effect on this endpoint: InitiativeAgentDataController::getInitiatives() never reads GetInitiativesQuery::getShouldIncludeConversionLabels(), and InitiativeAgentDataService::getInitiatives() has no parameter for it. Conversions are already returned inline on every business goal regardless of this value -- this flag does not gate them here (it does on GET /initiatives).

includeAssets.description: When true, each business goal's `assets` object is populated with its linked automations, campaigns, forms and SMS broadcasts. When false (default), `assets` is still present on every business goal but every list inside it is empty.

useOverviewConfig.description: When true, results are restricted to and ordered by the account's configured goals overview sort order (falling back to favorited goals), instead of the normal paginated listing.

orders.description: A single column-to-direction mapping, e.g. `orders[created_timestamp]=DESC`. Only the first key is honored if more than one is supplied. Column must be one of `folder`, `updated_timestamp`, `created_timestamp`; direction is case-insensitive and normalized to `ASC`/`DESC`.

filters.description: A field-to-value map applied as additional equality filters, e.g. `filters[source]=1`. `goal_type`, `goal_value` and `conversion_target_status` resolve against the goal's linked conversion folder; every other key filters the business goal's own record directly. Keys are restricted to the set below and an unlisted key is rejected with 422. Empty string and null values are ignored.

actions.name: get_business_goal_data
actions.description: Retrieve a business goal (agent-oriented read). A read-optimized, single-record view of one business goal, separate from GET /initiatives/{initiativeId}. Returned directly from InitiativeAgentDataService::getInitiative(). Unlike the list endpoint, assets are always populated here (no includeAssets flag), and each conversion's conversionEvents (trigger detail) is always included when present.

actions.description: Create a calendar feed.

title.description: Title of the calendar feed

notification.description: Whether or not this calendar has notifications

actions.description: List all calendar feeds.

actions.description: Retrieve a calendar feed.

id.description: ID of the calendar feed to retrieve

actions.name: update_calendar
actions.description: Update a calendar feed.

id.description: ID of the calendar feed to update

title.description: Title of the calendar feed

actions.name: create_campaign
actions.description: Create Campaign.

name.description: Name of the campaign. Required and must not be empty.

type.description: Type of the campaign. Required; one of single, recurring, split, responder, reminder, special, activerss or text.

canSplitContent.description: Whether the campaign can split its content. Stored as the campaign split_content flag; false when omitted.

actions.name: create_campaign_message
actions.description:
Create a campaign message. Associate a message with a campaign, which is the association a split (A/B) campaign uses to send more than one message.

`campaignid` is required; a request without it is a `400`.

Only `campaignid`, `messageid` and `percentage` may be written. Every other field of a campaign message is a counter maintained by the sending code, and is ignored when it is submitted.

The request needs the campaigns feature to be enabled for the account, and the caller has to have access to the campaign, otherwise the request is a `403`. A body without a `campaignMessage` object is a `400`.

campaignMessage.description: The link between the campaign and one of its messages.

campaignid.description: Id of the campaign the message belongs to.

messageid.description: Id of the message the campaign sends.

Submitting a `campaignid` moves the message to that campaign, which requires access to both the campaign the message belongs to and the campaign it is moved to.

Only `campaignid`, `messageid` and `percentage` may be written. Every other field of a campaign message is a counter maintained by the sending code, and is ignored when it is submitted.

actions.description:
Delete multiple campaigns. Delete several campaigns in one call. This is the v3 equivalent of the v1 `campaign_delete_list` action.

The body selects what to delete, in one of three shapes:

- `{"ids": [1, 2]}` — the given campaigns
- `[1, 2]` — a bare array of ids, equivalent to the above
- `{"deleteFirst": 5}` — the oldest N campaigns in the account, where N is between 1 and 10

`ids` and `deleteFirst` are mutually exclusive.

Deletion is not transactional: campaigns are removed one at a time, so a call can partially succeed. `deleted` lists the ids that were removed and `failed` the ids that were not, each with a reason. When nothing at all could be removed the request answers `404`.

This is the v3 equivalent of looping over `POST /api/3/contact/sync`, and it is the endpoint to reach for when a v1 integration synced contacts one request at a time.

The work is done in the background. The response is a `202` carrying the id of the process that was created, and the contacts are written after the response is sent, so a contact read back immediately afterwards may not reflect the request yet.

A request holding more than 250 contacts is rejected as a whole and no process is created. Rows are ...

contacts.description: The contacts to upsert, at most 250 per request.

email.description: Email address the contact is matched on. A row without an email is skipped.

fields.description: Custom field values for the contact, given as field id and value pairs.

field.description: Id of the custom field.

value.description: The value to store.

orgid.description: ID of the account to associate the contact with.

orgname.description: Name of an account to find or create; the contact is added to it.

open_tracking_optout.description: 1 when the contact has opted out of open pixel tracking, 0 when not.

urlParams.description: Query-string parameters are merged into this object by the handler.

service.description: salesforce records each newly created contact as sourced from Salesforce; any other value has no effect.

actions.name: bulk_edit_contacts
actions.description:
Bulk edit contacts. Starts a background job that applies one set of changes to many contacts: add or remove tags, lists and automations, add contacts to automation blocks, set field values, or queue contact enrichment. It serves the bulk edit screen in the app.

The body names the changes and which contacts they apply to. The contacts are either the ones in `contactIds`, or every contact that matches the filters (`listid`, `tagid`, `status`, `search`, `segmentid` and the others), which mean the same as the GET /contacts filters of the same name. The request body description says which filters apply together.

The request is checked first, the same way as POST /contact/bulk_update/validati...

scope.description: Which contacts a web app request means: `ids` (the contacts in `contactIds` or `ids`), `filter` (the contacts matching the filters, which must include at least one usable filter) or `all` (every contact; no `contactIds`, no `ids` and no filters allowed). A web app request without a matching scope is refused with 400 and nothing is changed. API key requests may leave it out.

toTagIds.description: Ids of contact tags to add. Unknown ids are skipped with a warning.

fromTagIds.description: Ids of contact tags to remove. Unknown ids are skipped with a warning.

toTags.description: Names of tags to add. A tag that does not exist yet is created, which needs permission to manage tags. It is created while the request is checked, so it exists even if a later check then fails the request.

fromTags.description: Names of tags to remove. Names that match no tag are ignored.

toListIds.description: Ids of lists to subscribe the contacts to. Unknown ids are skipped with a warning. A list the user may not access is reported as a warning too, but the contacts are still subscribed to it.

fromListIds.description: Ids of lists to unsubscribe the contacts from. Unknown ids are skipped with a warning. A list the user may not access is reported as a warning too, but the contacts are still unsubscribed from it.

toAutomationIds.description: Ids of active automations to add the contacts to. Unknown or inactive automations are skipped with a warning.

fromAutomationIds.description: Ids of automations to remove the contacts from. Only contacts currently in the automation are affected.

toAutomationBlockIds.description: Ids of automation blocks to add the contacts to, starting the automation at that block.

replayAction.description: Enter the contacts at the blocks in `toAutomationBlockIds` as a replay of that step. Needs at least one block id, blocks that support replay, and automations that are active and not holding new entries.

fieldValueUpdates.description: Values to set, keyed by custom field id. Also accepts `phone` and `userid` (the contact owner), and `customer_acct_name` (or `orgname`) with an object `{"id": 12, "name": "Example Inc"}` to set the account. The name decides: a name other than the contact's current account name is matched to an account by name, and created if none exists, whatever the id, so it must match the account's name exactly. Id 0 with an empty name, or with the contact's current account name, removes the contact's account. The account is ignored when the Accounts feature is off. Unknown field ids are skipped with a warning.

enrichContacts.description: Queue contact data enrichment for every contact covered. Needs contact data enrichment on the account, permission to edit contacts, and someone on the account to have agreed to the contact enrichment terms.

contactIds.description: Ids of the contacts to edit. When set, `listid`, `tagid`, `status`, `search`, `segmentid` and `segment_run_id` are ignored, but a request that sends both `q` and `search` is still refused.

ids.description: Another name for `contactIds`, with the same values and meaning. Send the ids in one or the other, not both. An empty list counts as not sent.

listid.description: Only contacts on this list. -1 means contacts on any list and -2 contacts on no list; 0, the default, does not filter.

tagid.description: Only contacts with this tag, or with any of a list of tags. -1 means contacts with any tag and -2 contacts with no tags; 0, the default, does not filter.

status.description: Only contacts with this list status, as in GET /contacts. -1, the default, means any status.

formid.description: Only contacts that came in through this form.

finishedAutomation.description: With `seriesid`: 1 for contacts that finished the automation, 0 for contacts still in it.

waitid.description: Only contacts waiting in this automation block.

customer_account.description: Only contacts that belong to this account, by account id.

search.description: Only contacts matching this search, as in GET /contacts. Not allowed together with `segmentid`.

q.description: Older name for `search`. Send one or the other, not both.

segmentid.description: Only contacts in this segment. The segment is run when the request is checked.

segment_run_id.description: A segment run to reuse, as returned in `runId` by POST /contact/bulk_update/validation. Needs `segmentid`.

actions.name: check_contact_bulk_edit_before_running_it
actions.description:
Check a contact bulk edit before running it. Checks a bulk edit the same way POST /contact/bulk_update does, and reports how many contacts it would touch. It does not start the edit. The app calls it before a bulk edit, to show the count and any problems.

It is not read-only: tags named in `toTags` that do not exist yet are created during the check (see `toTags`).

A request from a web app session must say which contacts it means in the `scope` query parameter. Requests authenticated with an API key or a service token are not checked.

The answer is 200 when there are no errors and 422 when there is at least one. Warnings alone do not fail the request. Ids that do not exist are dropped a...

scope.description: Which contacts a web app request means: `ids` (the contacts in `contactIds` or `ids`, which must not be empty), `filter` (the contacts matching the filters, at least one of which must actually narrow the selection), or `all` (every contact; the body must then carry no ids and no filters). A missing or mismatched scope fails with `errors.scope`. Ignored for API key and service requests.

toTagIds.description: Ids of contact tags to add. Unknown ids are skipped with a warning.

fromTagIds.description: Ids of contact tags to remove. Unknown ids are skipped with a warning.

toTags.description: Names of tags to add. A tag that does not exist yet is created, which needs permission to manage tags. It is created while the request is checked, so it exists even if a later check then fails the request.

fromTags.description: Names of tags to remove. Names that match no tag are ignored.

toListIds.description: Ids of lists to subscribe the contacts to. Unknown ids, and lists the user may not access, are reported as warnings.

fromListIds.description: Ids of lists to unsubscribe the contacts from. Unknown ids, and lists the user may not access, are reported as warnings.

toAutomationIds.description: Ids of active automations to add the contacts to. Unknown or inactive automations are skipped with a warning.

fromAutomationIds.description: Ids of automations to remove the contacts from. Only contacts currently in the automation are affected.

toAutomationBlockIds.description: Ids of automation blocks to add the contacts to, starting the automation at that block.

replayAction.description: Enter the contacts at the blocks in `toAutomationBlockIds` as a replay of that step. Needs at least one block id, blocks that support replay, and automations that are active and not holding new entries.

The name decides which account is linked, so it must match the account's name: a name different from the contact's current one is matched to an account by name, whatever the id, and a new account is created if none matches. Sending id 0 with an empty name, or with the contact's current account name, removes the contact's account. Unknown field ids are skipped with a warning.

enrichContacts.description: Queue contact data enrichment for every contact covered. Needs contact data enrichment on the account, permission to edit contacts, and someone on the account to have agreed to the contact enrichment terms.

tagid.description: Only contacts with this tag, or with any of a list of tags. -1 means contacts with any tag and -2 contacts with no tags; 0, the default, does not filter.

status.description: Only contacts with this list status, as in GET /contacts. -1, the default, means any status.

formid.description: Only contacts that came in through this form.
