actions.name: merge_contacts
actions.description:
Merge two contacts. Merges one contact into another and deletes the contact that was merged. The destination contact survives and keeps its id; the source contact's lists, tags, automations, deals, notes and activity are moved onto the destination, and the source is then removed.

The merge runs synchronously, so the response means the contacts have already been merged. It cannot be undone.

Where the two contacts hold conflicting information, `resolutionFieldId` and `resolutionAutomationId` name which of the two contacts wins: field values are taken from the contact named by `resolutionFieldId`, and automation membership from the contact named by `resolutionAutomationId`.

Requires the `...

source.description: Id of the contact to merge in. This contact is deleted once the merge completes.

destination.description: Id of the contact that survives the merge.

resolutionFieldId.description: Id of the contact whose field values win where both contacts hold a value. Must be the `source` or the `destination`.

resolutionAutomationId.description: Id of the contact whose automation membership wins where both contacts are in the same automation. Must be the `source` or the `destination`.

actions.name: create_or_update_contact
actions.description: Create or update a contact by email (upsert). Create or update a single contact by email address (upsert). When a contact with the given email already exists it is updated and the response is 200; otherwise a new contact is created and the response is 201, so the status code tells you which happened. Use this whenever the request supplies email addresses that may already be in the account, including pasted or imported lists, or to update a contact without knowing its id. Unlike POST /contacts, it never fails with a duplicate-email error. How the contact is found: with the lookupByAcId query parameter and contact.id, by id first. With contact.whatsapp_id, by WhatsApp id and then by email. ...

lookupByAcId.description: Set to true to find the contact by contact.id before any other lookup. If no contact has that id, the other lookups are used.

contact.description: The contact to create or update.

email.description: The contact's email address, used to find the contact. Required unless allowNullEmail applies or whatsapp_id is sent; without it the request fails with 400. Sending whatsapp_id instead needs a WhatsApp inbox and phone-only contacts on the account. Line breaks are removed, and so are spaces at either end.

phone.description: The contact's phone number. Must be a string; a number fails with 422. Used to find the contact when no email and no whatsapp_id are sent; if several contacts have this phone, the request fails with 400.

fieldValues.description: Custom field values to save with the contact. Each item sets one field. Fields you leave out are not changed.

field.description: Id of the custom field.

value.description: The new value. Lists are only supported for checkbox and listbox fields. For those fields, a string with the options separated by || also works.

orgid.description: Deprecated: use account. Id of the account to link the contact to.

id.description: Id of the contact to update. Used only with the lookupByAcId query parameter.

allowNullEmail.description: Set to true to sync a contact without an email address. Works only when the account has phone-only contacts turned on; then either email or phone must be sent, or the request fails with 400, and without an email the contact is found by phone. When phone-only contacts are off, an email is still required.

whatsapp_id.description: The contact's WhatsApp user id from Meta. When sent, the contact is found by this id first and then by email, and the email is optional. Needs a WhatsApp inbox on the account, or the request fails with 400, and phone-only contacts turned on, or it fails with 422.

account.description: Account to link the contact to, named by exactly one of id or name.

id.description: ID of an existing account; a missing account is refused.

name.description: Exact name of the account.

createIfMissing.description: Only with name: create the account when no account has that name. Refused with id.

account_name.description: Name of an account to find or create and link the contact to, when neither account nor organization is sent and the Accounts feature is on.

organization.description: Legacy alternative to account: ID of the account to link; ignored when account is sent.

channelIdentities.description: Channel identities that identify the contact and are attached to it. Only used when the account has channel identity contacts enabled.

disableAccountMatch.description: true turns off automatic account matching when the sync creates a new contact; no effect when it updates one.

fields.description: Alternative to fieldValues; ignored when fieldValues is sent.

field.description: Id of the custom field.

value.description: The new value.

form.description: ID of a form; the contact is also subscribed to the form's lists.

ip4.description: IPv4 address recorded as the contact's opt-in IP.

lists.description: List memberships to write for the contact.

list.description: ID of the list; must exist.

sdate.description: Subscribe date, as 'Y-m-d H:i:s' or 'Y-m-d' (start of that day). Defaults to now.

sendInstantAutoresponder.description: Send the list's instant autoresponders even for a membership that already existed or was unsubscribed. Cannot be true with suppressInstantAutoresponder.

suppressInstantAutoresponder.description: Do not send the list's instant autoresponders for this membership.

sendLastCampaign.description: Send the list's last campaign even when the list does not do so on subscribe.

open_tracking_optout.description: 1 when the contact has opted out of open pixel tracking, 0 when not.

tags.description: Tag names to add to the contact; missing tags are created.

source.description: Recorded as the source of the request for the webhooks the change fires.

actions.name: list_archived_contacts
actions.description: List archived contacts. The archived contacts of the account: contacts that were deleted and are kept for 360 days before they are purged. GET /contacts never returns them, whatever its status value; they are read here, or one at a time with GET /contactArchives/{id}. Only contacts archived within the last 360 days are listed, and only to API users in the Admin group: any other user gets 404. Each row is the contact as it was when archived, with the contact's fields plus deleted_at, when it was archived, and is_restorable, true when the contact is old enough to restore (archived at least 30 days ago by default; support can change an account's threshold) and not yet past the 360-day window...

search.description: Text to search for. A full email address matches the archived contact's email exactly. Any other single word is matched anywhere in email, first name, last name or phone. Several words are matched together against the full name, or as a whole against the phone. A single word that is not an email address is not combined with start, end or the 360-day limit (known defect); a two-word search or an exact email address is.

start.description: Only contacts archived on or after this moment, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Rounded down to the start of that day. A value earlier than 360 days ago is raised to 360 days ago, the oldest archive the API serves.

end.description: Only contacts archived on or before this moment, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Rounded up to the end of that day; a value in the future is capped at now.

filters[cdate].description: Exact creation date and time of the contact, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.

filters[udate].description: Exact last-modified date and time of the contact, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.

filters[userid].description: Id of the account user who owned the contact.

filters[deleted_at].description: Exact archive date and time, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. For a range use start and end.

orders[email].description: Order by email address (the default, ascending).

orders[name].description: Order by first name then last name.

orders[cdate].description: Order by when the contact was created.

orders[udate].description: Order by when the contact record was last changed.

orders[deleted_at].description: Order by when the contact was archived; desc lists the most recently archived first.

limit.description: Number of archived contacts to return per request. Defaults to 20; the maximum is 100, and asking for more is capped at 100.

offset.description: Number of archived contacts to skip before returning results. Use with limit to page.

meta.description: Set to omit to leave the metadata (total) out of the response.

actions.name: permanently_delete_several_archived_contacts
actions.description: Permanently delete several archived contacts. Removes up to 100 archived contacts for good in one request. They can no longer be restored or listed. Only API users in the Admin group may call this; any other user gets 404. The body is a JSON object with ids, a list of one to one hundred archived contact ids as integers. Ids that are already gone are skipped. Returns 200 with an empty object.

ids.description: The archived contact ids to delete, one to one hundred positive integers.

actions.name: restore_matching_archived_contacts
actions.description: Restore all matching archived contacts. Queues a restore of every archived contact that matches the body, the same selection the app's Archived contacts view makes with "Restore all". Only API users in the Admin group may call this; any other user gets 404. The body is required: send {} to restore every archived contact inside the restore window; an empty body is refused with 400. start and end narrow the archive date; the restore rounds them out to whole days in UTC. search narrows the selection by email, name or phone. Known defect: when search has several words, start and end limit only the contacts it matches by phone, not the ones it matches by name; the 360-day limit still applies t...

start.description: Only contacts archived on or after the start of this day (UTC), given as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. The too-recent check runs from the exact moment instead. A value earlier than 360 days ago is raised to 360 days ago. Ignored when not a number.

end.description: Only contacts archived on or before the end of this day (UTC), given as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. The too-recent check runs up to the exact moment instead. Defaults to now. Ignored when not a number.

search.description: Text to search for. A full email address matches exactly; any other single word is matched anywhere in email, first name, last name or phone; several words are matched together against the full name, or as a whole against the phone. The too-recent check described above uses only the email part of this match. With several words, start and end do not limit name matches (known defect).

actions.name: list_running_contact_restores
actions.description: List running contact restores. The account's contact restores that are still running: requests that have not finished, matched at least one contact, and were made in the last 30 days. A finished restore is not listed; read it with GET /contactArchives/restoreRequest/{id}. Only API users in the Admin group may call this; any other user gets 404. meta.total is the number of requests listed. While this list is not empty, POST /contactArchives/restoreRequest and POST /contactArchives/restoreAll return 409.

actions.name: restore_archived_contacts_by_id
actions.description: Restore archived contacts by id. Queues a restore of the archived contacts with the given ids. The contacts come back in the background, so the response only confirms the request; follow it with GET /contactArchives/restoreRequest/{id}. Only API users in the Admin group may call this; any other user gets 404. Every id must be an archived contact inside the restore window (see is_restorable on GET /contactArchives), or the whole request is refused with 400. When two selected archived contacts have the same email address, only the one with the highest id (normally the most recently archived) is restored. An empty ids list is accepted: it returns 201 and creates a restore request that matche...

ids.description: Ids of the archived contacts to restore, as listed by GET /contactArchives.

actions.name: get_contact_restore
actions.description: Retrieve a contact restore. The progress of one contact restore, running or finished. The restore is finished when finished_at is set; contacts_restored, contacts_failed and contacts_to_be_skipped then add up to contacts_matching. Only API users in the Admin group may call this; any other user gets 404. An id that does not exist, or that belongs to another account, returns 500, not 404.

id.description: The restore request id, from restoreRequestId in the response that created it or from GET /contactArchives/restoreRequest.

actions.name: get_archived_contact
actions.description: Retrieve an archived contact. One archived contact by the id it had before it was archived. The row is the contact as it was when archived, with deleted_at saying when. Unlike the list, this read is not limited to Admin users, has no 360-day limit, and carries no is_restorable flag. Returns 404 if no archived contact has that id, including when the contact is still active or has been permanently deleted.

id.description: The archived contact's id, as listed by GET /contactArchives.

actions.name: permanently_delete_archived_contact
actions.description: Permanently delete an archived contact. Removes an archived contact for good. The contact can no longer be restored or listed. Only API users in the Admin group may call this; any other user gets 404. Returns 200 with an empty object, also when the id was already gone, so a repeated delete is harmless. To remove several at once, use POST /contactArchives/deleteList.

id.description: The archived contact's id, as listed by GET /contactArchives.

actions.name: list_contact_automation_history_entries
actions.description: List all contact automation history entries. Lists the history entries kept for contacts' runs through automations, across the whole account. For most runs this is not the full step history: only some kinds of steps, such as waits, goals and sends, keep an entry here. For the full step history of one run, use GET /automations/{seriesId}/contactAutomations/{contactAutomationId}/steps. To read one run's entries, use GET /contactAutomations/{id}/automationLogs. The list has no filters or sort options, and entries come in no guaranteed order. Page with limit and offset, or fetch specific entries with ids.

limit.description: Number of entries to return. Defaults to 20; values above 100 are treated as 100.

offset.description: Number of entries to skip. Use with limit to page through the entries.

ids.description: Comma-separated entry IDs to return. When set, only those entries are returned; limit does not apply, but offset still does.

actions.name: retrieve_contact_automation_history_entry
actions.description: Retrieve a contact automation history entry. Returns one history entry by its ID. Each entry records one step of a contact's run through an automation. For most runs only some kinds of steps, such as waits, goals and sends, keep an entry here. Returns 404 if no entry has the id.

id.description: ID of the history entry.

actions.name: remove_contact_from_automation_by_ids
actions.description: Remove a contact from an automation by contact and automation. Removes the contact's active entry in the automation, identified by the contact (`contact` ID or `contact_email`) and the automation ID, without needing the contactAutomation ID. Only an active entry is removed; a completed entry is left as history. Use `DELETE /contactAutomations/{id}` when the contactAutomation ID is known.

automation.description: ID of the automation to remove the contact from

contact.description: ID of the contact. Required unless `contact_email` is given; ignored when `contact_email` is given.

contact_email.description: Email address of the contact. Takes precedence over `contact` when both are given.

actions.name: list_automations_contact_is_in
actions.description: List all automations a contact is in. Lists contacts' runs through automations, one entry per time a contact entered an automation, 20 per page by default and at most 100 per page (limit). Without a filter it covers every run in the account; users outside the Admin group only see runs of contacts on a list their group may access, or on no list. Each entry carries the run's status and progress. Runs that have ended may also be described in subscriberSeriesEnds. For one contact's runs, use GET /contacts/{id}/contactAutomations. This call does not refuse unknown filters or orderings; it ignores them.

actions.name: add_contact_to_automation
actions.description: Add a contact to an automation, or to several at once, so it enters the workflow and starts moving through its actions. An add through the API counts as added manually, so the automation's setting for how often a contact may enter does not apply: adding the same contact again starts another run instead of failing, up to 100 adds per contact per automation in 24 hours, after which the call answers 403. Only an active automation (status 1) is guaranteed to accept contacts. A draft (0) or inactive (2) automation answers 422 "The automation you have selected is inactive." for every contact, and so does a paused (3) one unless the account's automations accept entries while paused, so check the...

contactAutomation.description: Which contact to add, and to which automations.

contact.description: Id of the contact to add. Send this or contact_email. An existing contact's email address or 32-character hash is also accepted here; unlike contact_email, this never creates a contact, and an unknown value answers 422.

contact_email.description: Email address of the contact to add, instead of contact. When no contact has this address one is created with it first, which needs permission to add contacts and counts against the account's contact limit; the new contact stays even if the add then fails.

automation.description: Id of the automation to add the contact to. Send this or automations.

automations.description: Ids of up to 25 automations to add the contact to in one call, instead of automation. Each is added on its own; meta.succeeded and meta.failed in the response list the ids that did and did not take the contact.

actions.name: get_automation_contact_is_in
actions.description: Retrieve an automation a contact is in. Returns one run of a contact through an automation, with its status and progress. If the run has ended, subscriberSeriesEnds may say how. Users outside the Admin group can only read runs of contacts on a list their group may access, or on no list.

id.description: ID of the contactAutomation to retrieve

actions.name: update_contact_automation
actions.description: Update a contact automation. Ends a contact's run through an automation. `status` is the only writable field. Sending `completed: true` also cancels any wait the contact is scheduled for in that automation and records the end as cancelled through the API; send it together with `status: 2`. PATCH /contactAutomations/{id} is also accepted and does the same, with the same body and responses.

id.description: ID of the contactAutomation to update

status.description: 1 = active, 2 = completed

completed.description: When true, cancels pending waits for this contact in the automation and records the end. Not stored; send with `status: 2`.

actions.name: remove_contact_from_automation
actions.description: Remove a contact from an automation. Deletes a contact's run through an automation, so the contact no longer shows as being in it. The run's start records go with it. This call does not record an end or send a cancel for waits the contact is scheduled for. To stop a run and keep it as history, use PUT /contactAutomations/{id} with status 2 and completed true instead. Needs permission to edit contacts.

id.description: ID of the contactAutomation to delete

actions.name: retrieve_automation_of_contact_automation
actions.description: Retrieve the automation of a contact automation. Returns the automation this run is in, under automation. The body is an empty object {} when that automation no longer exists. Returns 404 if the run does not exist.

id.description: ID of the contactAutomation (the run)

actions.name: list_history_of_contact_automation
actions.description: List the history of a contact automation. Returns the history entries kept for this run, under contactAutomationLogs. For most runs this is not the full step history: only some kinds of steps, such as waits, goals and sends, keep an entry here. For the full step history, use GET /automations/{seriesId}/contactAutomations/{contactAutomationId}/steps. The list is not paged. The order is not guaranteed. Returns 404 if the run does not exist.

id.description: ID of the contactAutomation (the run)

actions.name: retrieve_contact_of_contact_automation
actions.description: Retrieve the contact of a contact automation. Returns the contact on this run, under contact. The body is an empty object {} when the contact no longer exists. Users outside the Admin group also get {} when the contact is only on lists their group may not access. Returns 404 if the run does not exist.

id.description: ID of the contactAutomation (the run)

actions.name: list_goals_reached_in_contact_automation
actions.description: List the goals reached in a contact automation. Returns the automation goals the contact reached in this run, under contactGoals. The list is not paged. The order is not guaranteed. Returns 404 if the run does not exist.

id.description: ID of the contactAutomation (the run)

actions.name: retrieve_how_contact_automation_ended
actions.description: Retrieve how a contact automation ended. Returns the record of how this run ended, under subscriberSeriesEnd. actions.name: list_contact_conversion_points
actions.description: List all contact conversion points. A contact conversion point is one touchpoint: something a contact did or received before converting, such as an email open, a link click, a delivered SMS or a site visit. Revenue from the conversion is attributed to these touchpoints. The app writes them when a contact converts, from the contact's recent activity. Filter by contact or type. Without an order, points come in no guaranteed order. Page with limit and offset, or fetch specific points with ids. Returns 403 when the account does not have Attribution.

filters[subscriberid].description: Return only points for this contact id. Exact match.

filters[type].description: Return only points of this type, such as LinkData. Exact match.

orders[tstamp].description: Sort by time. DESC, in any case, sorts high to low; any other value sorts low to high.

actions.name: retrieve_contact_conversion_point
actions.description: Retrieve a contact conversion point. A contact conversion point is one touchpoint: something a contact did or received before converting, such as an email open, a link click, a delivered SMS or a site visit. Revenue from the conversion is attributed to these touchpoints. The app writes them when a contact converts, from the contact's recent activity. Returns one point by its id. Returns 404 if no point has the id, and 403 when the account does not have Attribution.

An attribution gives part of a conversion's revenue to the campaign or message behind the touchpoint. The id is the id of the point. The response is not paged, and the attributions come in no guaranteed order. attributions is an empty array when there are none. Returns 404 if no point has the id, and 403 when the account does not have Attribution.

id.description: Id of the point.

actions.name: retrieve_contact_of_contact_conversion_point
actions.description: Retrieve the contact of a contact conversion point. Returns the contact that one point belongs to. The id is the id of the point, not of the contact. Returns an empty object {} when the contact no longer exists or the point has none. Returns 404 if no point has the id, and 403 when the account does not have Attribution.

id.description: Id of the point.

It is added when one of the conversion's triggers fires for the contact, for example a tracked event, a visited URL, an automation step or an e-commerce order. It keeps the amount and currency booked at that moment. The list shows only entries whose conversion is visible. It leaves out hidden conversions, such as the built-in e-commerce reporting conversion. Entries with no order are left out when the account lacks deals, e-commerce data or site messages, or the API user's group lacks the deals permission. Entries made by an order are left out when the account lacks e-commerce data. Filter ...

actions.name: list_activities_of_contact_conversion

actions.name: list_attributions_of_contact_conversion

The ga_campaign_*, ga_first_visit, ga_times_visited,...

actions.name: get_secondary_contact
actions.description: Retrieve a secondary contact. Returns one link between a contact and a deal by the link's id. It can be a primary-contact link as well as a secondary one. lastContactDate and lastContactType are not included here. Needs the deals permission; 404 when no link has this id.

id.description: Id of the link (the contactDeal id), not the contact or deal id.

actions.name: update_contact_deals

Only the properties present in the request change. Changing contact removes the previous contact's score values for the deal and logs the change on the deal. Changing deal moves the link only: neither deal records an activity and the previous deal keeps its score values. Changing role is recorded as a deal activity. 404 if no secondary contact has this id; 422 if contact or deal is emptied or names a record that does not exist. Needs the deals permission.

id.description: Secondary Contact's id

contactDeal.description: The link to create or change.

contact.description: Id of the contact.

actions.description: Delete a secondary contact. Removes a contact from a deal by the link's id. The deal and the contact themselves are not deleted. id.description: Id of the link (the contactDeal id), not the contact or deal id.

actions.name: list_contact_emails
actions.description: List contact emails. Lists the one-to-one emails that users sent to contacts, for example from a contact or deal page in ActiveCampaign, or logged by the ActiveCampaign Chrome extension for Gmail. actions.name: retrieve_contact_email
actions.description: Retrieve a contact email. Returns a single one-to-one email record that a user sent to a contact. The subject and body are on the linked message, not in the record. Returns 404 if no email record has the id.

actions.name: list_contact_goal_list_entries

actions.name: retrieve_reached_goal_of_contact_goal_list_entry

orders[subscribergoalid].description: Sort by reached goal id. DESC, in any case, sorts high to low; any other value sorts low to high.

limit.description: Number of entries to return. Defaults to 20; values above 100 are treated as 100.

offset.description: Number of entries to skip. Use with limit to page through the entries.

ids.description: Comma-separated entry ids to return. When set, only those entries are returned; limit does not apply, but offset still does.

actions.name: retrieve_contact_goal_tag_entry
actions.description: Retrieve a contact goal tag entry. A contact goal tag entry records one tag the contact had when it reached an automation goal. Returns one entry by its id. Returns 404 if no entry has the id.

id.description: ID of the entry.

actions.name: retrieve_reached_goal_of_contact_goal_tag_entry
actions.description: Retrieve the reached goal of a contact goal tag entry. Returns the reached goal that one entry belongs to: the contact, the automation, the goal and when it was reached. actions.name: list_goal_completions

actions.name: list_contact_import_log_rows

This endpoint returns every row in the account, with no way to narrow it to one import: filters and orders are ignored, and rows have no defined order. limit.description: Number of rows to return. Defaults to 20; values above 100 are treated as 100. A value of 0, a negative number or a non-numeric value returns every row and ignores offset.

offset.description: Number of rows to skip. Use with limit to page through the rows.

actions.description: Retrieve a contact import log row. One row of the contact import log, by its ID. Each row is one line of the log that imports write as they run: one row for each row processed, imported or not. When a contact was imported but list subscriptions were skipped, there is one row per skipped subscription instead (res 2). Imports started from the app's import tool, imports submitted through POST /import/bulk_import, older sync imports and integrations' automatic syncs all write rows here. To see how one import went, use the endpoint for its kind: for an import started from the app or by an integration, GET /import/history to find it (for an app import, its processid matches the processid on the...
