actions.name: list_contact_subscriptions_to_lists
actions.description: List contact subscriptions to lists. One row per contact-to-list subscription, carrying the contact id, the list id, the subscription status and its dates. Filter with contact to see every list one contact is on, with status to see the subscriptions in one state, with sourceIds to see the subscriptions created through given sources, for example imports, with filters[listid] to see one list, or with a date window to see when contacts joined or left. filters[subscribed_after] and filters[subscribed_before] bound sdate; filters[unsubscribed_after] and filters[unsubscribed_before] bound udate. All filters combine and meta.total counts the rows that match, so the number of contacts that unsubs...

contact.description: Return only the subscriptions of this contact id.

status.description: Return only subscriptions in this state: 0 unconfirmed, 1 active, 2 unsubscribed, 3 bounced.

sourceIds.description: Return only subscriptions created through these sources. Repeat the key for several values: sourceIds[]=1&sourceIds[]=5. A comma-separated value is not split: only its first number is used. Values: 0 unknown, 1 import, 2 sync, 3 account user, 4 API, 5 form, 6 form opt-in, 7 trigger, 8 SMS, 9 automation, 10 bulk edit, 11 email, 12 Gmail.

filters[listid].description: Return only the subscriptions to this list id. Must be a whole number; anything else returns 400. A blank or 0 is the same as leaving it out.

filters[subscribed_after].description: Return only subscriptions whose sdate is later than this date or time. The bound is exclusive. Any date or datetime that PHP strtotime reads works, such as 2026-10-01, 10/01/2026 or 2026-10-01T13:45:10-05:00; a blank or unreadable value returns 400. Without an offset the time is read in the time zone the dates in the response are shown in. sdate is reset when a contact resubscribes. It narrows meta.total as well as the page.

filters[subscribed_before].description: Return only subscriptions whose sdate is earlier than this date or time. The bound is exclusive, with the same formats, time zone and 400 as filters[subscribed_after]. For a calendar month, send the last instant of the month before as filters[subscribed_after] and the first instant of the next month as this.

filters[unsubscribed_after].description: Return only subscriptions whose udate is later than this date or time. The bound is exclusive, with the same formats, time zone and 400 as filters[subscribed_after]. udate is set when the status becomes unsubscribed or bounced, and is null while the subscription is active, so a window on it never returns active rows. Send status=2 to leave out bounces.

filters[unsubscribed_before].description: Return only subscriptions whose udate is earlier than this date or time. The bound is exclusive, with the same formats, time zone and 400 as filters[subscribed_after]. Rows with no udate are never returned. Send status=2 to leave out bounces.

limit.description: Number of subscription rows to return per request. Defaults to 20; the maximum is 100, and asking for more is capped at 100.

offset.description: Number of subscription rows to skip before returning results. Use with limit to page.

actions.name: add_contact_to_list
actions.description:
Update list status for a contact. Subscribes a contact to a list, or changes the status of the contact's subscription to it. If the contact already has a membership on the list, that membership is updated and the response is 200; otherwise a new one is created and the response is 201. Needs the permission to edit contacts.

If the contact's membership on the list is currently unsubscribed, any change to it needs the permission to resubscribe contacts, whatever status you send, including another unsubscribe. Without it the request fails with 422.

Any status other than 2 needs a contact that exists and a list that exists (404 otherwise), and a contact with an email address for an email lis...

list.description: Id of the list. Must be a positive number.

contact.description: Id of the contact. Must be a positive number.

status.description: 1 to subscribe, 2 to unsubscribe. 0 (unconfirmed) and 3 (bounced) are also accepted and stored as sent. See the operation description for what each does.

sourceid.description: With an API key this is stored as 4 (API) whatever you send, unless you send the number 8 (SMS), which is kept. The string "8" is stored as 4.

responder.description: 1 (the default) or 0. 0 stops the list's later, scheduled autoresponders for this membership. It does not stop the subscribe autoresponders sent at once when the membership is created; use suppressInstantAutoresponder for that.

sendInstantAutoresponder.description: Set to true to send the list's subscribe autoresponders even when the contact was already on the list or had unsubscribed. With status 2, sends the list's unsubscribe autoresponders instead. Does nothing for status 0 or 3, when the contact is excluded from the list, or when the account does not have Campaigns. Cannot be true together with suppressInstantAutoresponder. Accepts true, false, 1, 0 and the strings true, false, yes, no, on, off, 1 and 0, in any letter case. An empty string counts as false. Other values fail with 422.

suppressInstantAutoresponder.description: Set to true to not send the list's subscribe autoresponders when this request creates the membership. Accepts true, false, 1, 0 and the strings true, false, yes, no, on, off, 1 and 0, in any letter case. An empty string counts as false. Other values fail with 422.

sendLastCampaign.description: Set to true to send the contact the last campaign sent to the list, even when the list is not set up to do that. Only for status 1, and not when the contact is excluded from the list. Accepts true, false, 1, 0 and the strings true, false, yes, no, on, off, 1 and 0, in any letter case. An empty string counts as false. Other values fail with 422.

actions.name: get_contact_list_subscription
actions.description: Retrieve a contact list subscription. Returns one contact-to-list membership by its own ID. To find the ID, list subscriptions with `GET /contactLists?contact=` or follow `links.contactLists` on a contact.

id.description: ID of the contact list subscription (the contactList record, not the list)

actions.name: update_contact_list_subscription
actions.description: Update a contact list subscription. Updates one membership by its ID. `list`, `contact` and `status` must be sent and must match the record; `status` 2 unsubscribes, 1 re-subscribes. Re-subscribing a contact who unsubscribed requires the resubscribe permission and is refused for self-unsubscribes. Subscribing to an email list needs a contact with an email address, and to an SMS list a contact with a phone number. `POST /contactLists` does the same by list and contact without the record ID. To take a contact off a list, set `status` 2; the membership record is kept as consent history. PATCH /contactLists/{id} does the same thing.

id.description: ID of the contact list subscription (the contactList record, not the list)

list.description: ID of the list; must match the record

contact.description: ID of the contact; must match the record

status.description: 0 unconfirmed, 1 active, 2 unsubscribed, 3 bounced. Set 2 to unsubscribe and 1 to subscribe again.

sourceid.description: How the subscription was created; set 4 when re-subscribing through the API

responder.description: 1 to keep sending list autoresponders to this contact (default), 0 to suppress them for this membership

actions.name: list_contact_log_entries
actions.description: List all contact log entries. Lists the contact log entries in the account. merge is the only action written today: each merge of two contacts records one entry on the surviving contact. To read one contact's entries, use GET /contacts/{id}/contactLogs instead. The list has no filters or sort options, and entries come in no guaranteed order. Page with limit and offset, or fetch specific entries with ids.

limit.description: Number of entries to return. Defaults to 20; values above 100 are treated as 100.

offset.description: Number of entries to skip. Use with limit to page through the entries.

ids.description: Comma-separated log entry IDs to return. When set, only those entries are returned; limit does not apply, but offset still does.

actions.name: retrieve_contact_log_entry
actions.description: Retrieve a contact log entry. Returns one contact log entry by its ID. merge is the only action written today: each merge of two contacts records one entry on the surviving contact. Returns 404 if no log entry has the id.

id.description: ID of the log entry.

actions.name: list_contact_tag_associations
actions.description:
List all contact-tag associations. List the tags applied to contacts. Each item is a single contact-to-tag association, and its `id` is the value to pass to `DELETE /contactTags/{id}` when removing a tag from a contact.

Filter by contact, by tag, or by both to look up a specific association. Note that the filters use the underlying column names `subscriberid` and `tagid`, while the response returns the same values as `contact` and `tag` — `filters[contact]` and `filters[tag]` are not supported.

Unrecognized filter and order parameters are silently ignored, so a request with a misspelled filter looks successful while returning the unfiltered set.

Associations whose tag has since been de...

filters[subscriberid].description: Filter by the id of the contact the tag is applied to. This is the same value the response returns as `contact`.

filters[tagid].description: Filter by the id of the tag. This is the same value the response returns as `tag`.

filters[cdate].description: Return only associations applied at exactly this date and time, written YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS in the platform timezone, the one the response's other timestamps carry. This is an exact match: a date without a time matches nothing, and there is no range form. To find the tags applied since a date, filter by filters[tagid], order with orders[cdate]=desc and page until cdate passes the date. An operator suffix such as filters[cdate][gt] is applied as an exact match with that value, not as a range.

orders[cdate].description: Order results by the date the tag was applied to the contact.

orders[tagid].description: Order results by tag id, ascending or descending.

orders[subscriberid].description: Order results by contact id, ascending or descending.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of contactTag association ids to return. Overrides limit; offset still applies.

limit.description: The number of records to return for each call. Default is 20; maximum value is 100.

offset.description: Offset index of records to return.

actions.name: add_tag_to_contact
actions.description: Add a tag to contact. Applies one existing tag to one contact. contact is a contact id and tag is a tag id; they are different id spaces, so the tag id must come from GET /tags or POST /tags, never from a contact record. The response's contactTag id is the association id used by DELETE /contactTags/{id}. A new association returns 201. The contact is included under contacts; the tag definition is included under tags when activity logging is enabled for the account, so do not rely on it and fetch the tag from GET /tags/{id} if needed. In the 201 body, contact and tag inside contactTag are numbers as sent, while every other response returns them as strings. If the tag is already applied, the...

contactTag.description: The contact and the tag to apply to it.

contact.description: The contact id, from GET /contacts.

tag.description: The tag id, from GET /tags or POST /tags. Not the tag name, and not a contact id.

actions.name: get_contact_tag_association
actions.description: Retrieve a contact tag. Returns a single contact-to-tag association by its id. The contact and tag fields are ids; fetch the tag definition itself from GET /tags/{id}. Returns 404 if the association does not exist. No permission beyond API access is checked.

id.description: ID of the contactTag association to retrieve

actions.name: remove_tag_from_contact
actions.description: Remove a tag from a contact. Removes a tag from a contact by the contactTag association id (returned by GET /contactTags, POST /contactTags, or POST /contacts/{id}/tags). This is not the tag id. The tag definition itself is not deleted. Returns 404 if the association does not exist. To remove a tag by contact id and tag id or name instead, use DELETE /contacts/{id}/tags/{tagId} or DELETE /contacts/{id}/tags with the tag query parameter. Removing the tag starts the automations that start when this tag is removed, and sends the contact_tag_removed and contact updated webhooks. Requires the contact edit permission; users outside the main user group can only remove tags from contacts on their...

id.description: The contactTag id

actions.name: list_all_contacts
actions.description: List, search, and filter contacts. The read behind the Contacts page. It finds contacts by list (listid), tag (tagid, or filters[tagName] for a tag name), list status (status), text (search matches name, email, phone and account name), segment (segmentid), form (formid), automation (seriesid), or created and updated date (filters[created_after], filters[created_before], filters[updated_after], filters[updated_before]). Filters combine, except that while segmentid is set only status and search still apply and the other filters are ignored, and tagid and filters[tagName] cannot be sent together. GET /contactTags and GET /contactLists return association rows, not contacts. Use only the query...

ids.description: Return only the contacts with these ids. Pass a comma-separated list (ids=1,2,42) or repeat the key (ids[]=1&ids[]=2). The response returns at most as many contacts as ids given.

limit.description: Number of contacts to return per request. Defaults to 20; the maximum is 100, and asking for more is capped at 100.

offset.description: Number of contacts to skip before returning results. Use with limit to page through contacts. For walking a large set, filtering with id_greater is more reliable than a growing offset.

meta.description: Set to only to return just the metadata (such as the total count) with no contact records, or to omit to leave the metadata out of the response.

email.description: Email address of the contact you want to get

email_like.description: Filter contacts that contain the given value in the email address

exclude.description: Exclude the contact with the given ID from the response. Can be repeated to exclude multiple IDs: exclude[]=1&exclude[]=2.

formid.description: Filter contacts associated with the given form

id_greater.description: Only include contacts with an ID greater than the given ID

id_less.description: Only include contacts with an ID less than the given ID

listid.description: Filter contacts associated with the given list

phone.description: Filter contacts whose stored phone number starts with the given value, compared against the string exactly as stored, including country code, spaces, and punctuation (for example +1 555-555-5555). If the stored format is unknown, use search with one segment of the number (for example 5555) instead. A differently formatted phone value returns no matches, and search matches segments of the stored format (or a prefix of the last segment) but never a run of digits with the formatting stripped.

organization.description: (Deprecated) Please use Account-Contact end points. Filter contacts associated with the given organization ID

customer_account.description: Filter contacts that belong to the given account, by account id. Equivalent to organization.

search.description: Search contacts. A full email address matches the contact's email exactly; any other value is matched against email, first name, last name, phone, and account name. q is accepted as an alias. When search is set it takes precedence over email_like and filters[email_hash].

segmentid.description: Return only contacts that match a list segment. The first API call within 1 hour or an API call with the param `forceQuery=1` will kick off an new segment request. When the segment results are ready, subsequent API calls without the `forceQuery` param will return contacts that match the segment - timeout 1hr)

seriesid.description: Filter contacts associated with the given automation

finishedAutomation.description: Only used together with seriesid. Set to 1 to return only contacts that finished the automation, or 0 for contacts that entered it but have not finished.

conversionid.description: Only used together with seriesid. Return only contacts that hit the given conversion while they were in the automation.

status.description: Filter contacts by list-membership status: -1 any (the default), 0 unconfirmed, 1 active, 2 unsubscribed, 3 bounced. Combine with listid to check the status on one list. Values above 3 match nothing and return an empty result with total 0 rather than an error; values below -1 behave as "on at least one list, any status" (or "on the given listid, any status" when listid is set); a non-numeric value is read as 0 (unconfirmed).

tagid.description: Filter contacts associated with the given tag

filters[created_before].description: Filter contacts that were created prior to this date

filters[created_after].description: Filter contacts that were created after this date

filters[updated_before].description: Contacts whose record was last modified before this date. The last-modified date moves on any save of the contact record and, through database triggers, on list, tag, custom field, score, note and task changes however they are made, so it is not the date a list status changed and a window on it includes every contact touched for any reason. The time a contact left a list is udate on its list membership, which GET /contactLists filters with filters[unsubscribed_after] and filters[unsubscribed_before].

filters[updated_after].description: Contacts whose record was last modified after this date. The last-modified date moves on any save of the contact record and, through database triggers, on list, tag, custom field, score, note and task changes however they are made, so it is not the date a list status changed: a window on it includes every contact touched in that window for any reason. This endpoint has no filter for when a contact unsubscribed or bounced; that time is udate on the contact's list membership, which GET /contactLists filters with filters[unsubscribed_after] and filters[unsubscribed_before].

filters[id].description: Filter by exact contact id. To fetch several known contacts at once, prefer the ids parameter.

filters[email].description: Filter by exact email address. Equivalent to the email parameter.

filters[cdate].description: Filter contacts created at exactly the given date and time. For a range, use filters[created_before] and filters[created_after].

filters[udate].description: Filter contacts last updated at exactly the given date and time. For a range, use filters[updated_before] and filters[updated_after].

filters[email_hash].description: Filter contacts by the hash of their email address (the hash field returned on the contact). The top-level email_hash parameter is a deprecated alias. Ignored when search is supplied.

filters[tagName].description: Filter contacts by tag name instead of tag id. Accepts one tag name or a list (filters[tagName][]=a&filters[tagName][]=b); a contact matches if it has any of the tags. Cannot be combined with tagid. Unknown tag names are rejected with a 400 error.

filters[fields][{fieldId}].description: Filter contacts by custom field value, for example filters[fields][5]=blue. Repeat with different field ids to require all of them at once. On single-value fields the value matches from the start of the stored value; on multi-select fields (listbox, checkbox) it matches anywhere. An empty value matches contacts with a blank or missing value. Unknown field ids are rejected with a 400 error.

filters[first_name].description: Filter contacts whose first name is exactly the given value. Also accepted as filters[firstName].

filters[last_name].description: Filter contacts whose last name is exactly the given value. Also accepted as filters[lastName].

filters[userid].description: Filter contacts owned by the given user, by user id. Also accepted as filters[owner].

filters[orgname].description: Filter contacts whose account (organization) name is exactly the given value. Also accepted as filters[customer_acct_name].

filters[open_tracking_optout].description: Filter contacts by whether they have opted out of open pixel tracking: 1 for opted out, 0 for not.

waitid.description: Filter by contacts in the wait queue of an automation block

orders[name].description: Order contacts by full name. Applied as first name then last name, both in the given direction.

orders[score].description: Order contacts by score. Send the score id in sortId: each contact is then ranked by its highest value for that score, and contacts without one come last. sortId is not enforced. Without it the query joins every score value a contact has, which is slow on large accounts, drops contacts that have no score value, and can list a contact once per score value. orders[contactScoreValue] and orders[score_recent] are not order keys and are silently ignored.

orders[userid].description: Order contacts by contact owner (user id)

orders[orgname].description: Order contacts by the name of the account they belong to

orders[field].description: Order contacts by the value of a custom field. Use asc or desc and pass the custom field id in the sortId parameter.

in_group_lists.description: Set this to "true" in order to return only contacts that the current user has permissions to see.

forceQuery.description: If present and equal to 1, a new segment request is kicked off which will return an updated result set. Otherwise, a segmented API request with a consistent sorting will return the same results for 1 hour. Note that re-ordering the results will also cause an updated result set to be returned.

sortId.description: Id of the score (with orders[score]) or custom field (with orders[field]) to sort by. orders[field] is ignored without it; orders[score] still runs without it, see that parameter.

q.description: Alias for search; prefer search. When both are sent, q is used for the text search. Only search switches off email_like and filters[email_hash], and only search is applied inside a segment (segmentid) query; q is not.

sort.description: Shortcut for ordering by full name: sort=name orders contacts by first name, then last name, both ascending. Ignored when any orders[...] parameter is sent. For every other ordering, and for descending order, use the orders[...] parameters.

name.description: Used only together with email_like, and only when search is empty; on its own it does nothing. A contact then matches when its email contains the part of email_like before the @, or when its first and last name equal the first two words of name (name=Sam Example matches first name Sam and last name Example).

nameOrEmailLike.description: Older quick search kept for existing callers; prefer search. Matches contacts whose full name (first and last name joined by a space) or email contains the value anywhere. Applied even when search is also sent.

nameOrEmailOrPhoneLike.description: Like nameOrEmailLike, and also matches when the phone number contains the value anywhere. Prefer search.

actions.name: create_contact
actions.description: Create a contact. Create a brand-new contact. This endpoint fails with a 422 duplicate-email error when a contact with the same email address already exists; it never updates an existing contact. To add or import contacts that may already exist, use POST /contact/sync for one contact or POST /import/bulk_import for many (up to 250 per request) instead: both create or update by email, and the import can also set list subscriptions and tags per contact. The same request can also save custom field values (contact.fieldValues), add tags (contact.tags) and subscribe the contact to lists (contact.lists or contact.form). The user needs the add contacts permission. If your account uses social cha...

email.description: The contact's email address. Line breaks are removed, and so are spaces at either end. It must be valid and no other contact may have it, or the request fails with 422. Required on create, unless allowNullEmail applies. On update, leave it out to keep the current address.

phone.description: The contact's phone number. Must be a string; a number fails with 422.

allowNullEmail.description: Set to true to save the contact without an email address. This only works when the account has phone-only contacts turned on. The phone must then be unique, and is required unless the contact has a channel identity. When phone-only contacts are off, an email is still required. Leave email out or send null; an empty string still fails.

fieldValues.description: Custom field values to save with the contact. Each item sets one field. Fields you leave out are not changed. The saved values are returned in the top-level fieldValues array of the response.

field.description: Id of the custom field.

value.description: The new value. Lists are only supported for checkbox and listbox fields. For those fields, a string with the options separated by || also works.

fields.description: Deprecated: use fieldValues. The old name for fieldValues, with the same items. Ignored when fieldValues is sent.

items.description: A field and value, as in fieldValues.

field.description: Id of the custom field.

value.description: Value to store in the custom field, validated against the type of the field.

account.description: Links the contact to an account. Send either id or name, not both. Needs the Accounts feature and the edit contacts permission, or the request fails with 403. When sent, organization and account_name are ignored.

id.description: Id of an existing account. An id that does not exist fails with 422.

name.description: Name of the account. Spaces at either end and letter case do not matter. If no account has this name, the request fails with 422 unless createIfMissing is true.

createIfMissing.description: Only with name. Set to true to create the account when no account has the name. Creating needs the add accounts permission, or the request fails with 403. Defaults to false. The account is created before the contact is checked, so it stays even if the request then fails.

organization.description: Deprecated: use account. Id of the account to link the contact to. Ignored when account is sent.

account_name.description: Name of the account to link the contact to. The contact links to the account with this name, which is created if none has it. Used only when neither account nor organization is sent, and only when the account has the Accounts feature; otherwise ignored. The account is created before the contact is checked, so it stays even if the request then fails.

orgid.description: Deprecated: use account. Id of the account to link the contact to. If sent together with account or organization, orgid wins.

tags.description: Names of tags to add to the contact. A name that no tag has yet creates that tag. Tags the contact already has stay, and so do tags you leave out; this field never removes a tag. In each name, commas and line breaks become spaces, and HTML, emoji and spaces at either end are removed. A name that is then empty or longer than 250 characters fails with 422. New tags are created before the contact is checked, so they stay even if the request then fails.

lists.description: Lists to subscribe the contact to. Each list you name becomes an active subscription, also when the contact was unconfirmed or unsubscribed on it. The exception is a double opt-in form in contact.form; see form. Lists you leave out are not changed. A non-empty list needs the edit contacts permission, on create too, or the request fails with 403. All lists are checked before the contact is saved, and the contact is not saved if one fails. A list that does not exist, or an item with a key not listed here, fails with 422. So does resubscribing a contact who unsubscribed from the list, unless the user has the permission to resubscribe contacts. An email list needs a contact with an email address and an SMS list needs one with a phone number, or the request fails with 400. The mail options below do nothing while a subscription is unconfirmed.

sdate.description: When the subscription started, as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS or YYYY-MM-DD (start of that day). It is set even when the contact is already on the list. Leave it out to keep the current date; a new subscription, or one that becomes active again, then starts now. Any other format fails with 422.

sendInstantAutoresponder.description: Set to true to send the list's subscribe autoresponders even when the contact was already on the list or had unsubscribed. Cannot be true together with suppressInstantAutoresponder. Accepts true, false, 1, 0 and the strings true, false, yes, no, on, off, 1 and 0, in any letter case. An empty string counts as false. Other values fail with 422.

suppressInstantAutoresponder.description: Set to true to not send the list's subscribe autoresponders. Accepts true, false, 1, 0 and the strings true, false, yes, no, on, off, 1 and 0, in any letter case. An empty string counts as false. Other values fail with 422.

sendLastCampaign.description: Set to true to send the contact the last campaign sent to the list, even when the list is not set up to do that. Accepts true, false, 1, 0 and the strings true, false, yes, no, on, off, 1 and 0, in any letter case. An empty string counts as false. Other values fail with 422.

form.description: Id of a form. The write then acts like a submission of that form. The contact is also subscribed to the form's lists, with the same permission and checks as lists. If the form uses double opt-in, every list subscription this request creates stays unconfirmed, including lists named in contact.lists. The confirmation email is sent when one of the form's own lists gets a new subscription, and the form's actions and its submit automations run once the contact confirms. Otherwise they run now. An id that is not a form fails with 422.

ip4.description: The IPv4 address the contact signed up from. It is saved on the contact, where ip in the response shows it as a number, and on the list subscriptions this request creates. An address that is not IPv4, such as an IPv6 address, fails with 422. An empty string or null records nothing.

whatsapp_id.description: The contact's WhatsApp user id from Meta. Used only when the account has a WhatsApp inbox; otherwise it is dropped, and so is whatsapp_username when sent with it. It also needs phone-only contacts turned on, or the request fails with 422. With a whatsapp_id the email address is optional. If another contact already has this id, the request fails with 409.

whatsapp_username.description: The contact's WhatsApp username. Without a WhatsApp inbox it is dropped when sent with whatsapp_id, and saved when sent alone.

channelIdentities.description: Identities of this contact on connected messaging channels. Used only on accounts where channel identity contacts are enabled; ignored otherwise. The same source, channelAccountId and externalId may not appear twice in one request.

source.description: Messaging channel the identity belongs to: instagram or messenger.

channelAccountId.description: ID of the connected channel account the identity belongs to. At most 64 characters.

externalId.description: ID of the person on that channel. At most 255 characters.

open_tracking_optout.description: 1 when the contact has opted out of open pixel tracking, 0 when not. On PUT, sending 0 for a contact that has never answered (open_tracking_optout_updated_at is null) records the current time as its consent date; leave the field out to keep the contact unanswered.

disableAccountMatch.description: Set to true to skip automatic account matching for the new contact. Matching links a new contact to an account by its email domain. It only runs on ActiveCampaign's own internal account, so on other accounts this setting has no effect.

contact.description: The contact to create.

useDefaults.description: Accepted for compatibility with the custom field value endpoints; it has no effect when saving a contact.

actions.name: delete_multiple_contacts
actions.description:
Delete multiple contacts. Deletes several contacts in one call. This is the v3 equivalent of the v1 `contact_delete_list` action.

The body selects what to delete, in one of two shapes (the schema lists all three keys as optional; the API rejects a body with neither `ids` nor `deleteAll`):

- `{"ids": [1, 2]}` deletes the given contacts.
- `{"deleteAll": true}` deletes every contact that is actively subscribed to a list the caller can access.

`ids` and `deleteAll` are mutually exclusive. Either shape may add `listids` to limit the delete to those lists. The accessible lists are the lists the API user's group may manage; `listids` is narrowed to them.

A contact is removed from each affec...

ids.description: Ids of the contacts to delete. Positive integers; numeric strings are accepted and duplicates are ignored. `"_all"` is not accepted here; use `deleteAll` instead. Send `ids` or `deleteAll`, never both: a body with both keys is rejected with 400.

deleteAll.description: Must be `true`. Deletes every contact actively subscribed to the accessible lists, or to `listids` when given. Send `ids` or `deleteAll`, never both: a body with both keys is rejected with 400.

listids.description: Only remove the contacts from these lists. Positive integers; numeric strings are accepted. Omit to remove them from every accessible list.

actions.name: get_contact_notes
actions.description: Retrieve a contact's notes. The notes attached to one contact. Each note carries its text, the account user who wrote it (userid), and when it was created and last changed (cdate, mdate). Every note comes back in one response, drafts included (is_draft): limit, offset, filters and orders are ignored on this path, and no order is guaranteed, so sort on cdate yourself if order matters. To add a note to a contact, use POST /contacts/{contactId}/notes (create-a-contact-note). Returns 404 if the contact does not exist.

contactId.description: ID of the contact whose notes are returned

actions.name: create_note_on_contact
actions.description: Create a note on a contact. Adds a note to the contact named in the path. The path says which contact owns the note, so the body does not name one: owner and ownerType are dropped, and reltype and relid are replaced with the contact from the path. The author is the authenticated API user. Unless the note is a draft, the contact note webhook fires. Returns 404 when the contact does not exist, 422 when the body has no note object or its note text is missing or blank, 400 when listId is not a whole number of 0 or more, and 403 when the API user may not edit contacts.

contactId.description: ID of the contact the note is created on

note.description: The text of the note. Emoji are removed and HTML characters are escaped before it is saved.

is_draft.description: 0 or 1. 1 saves the note as a draft: the note webhook does not fire. Defaults to 0.

mentionStrings.description: Usernames to mention, each written as @username. Every matching user who is not already mentioned on this note gets a mention record and a notification. Not returned on the note.

listId.description: Id of the list whose contact-note webhooks fire for this note; 0, the default, fires the webhooks of every list. Not stored on the note. 400 when it is not a whole number of 0 or more.

actions.name: delete_note_from_contact
actions.description: Delete a note from a contact. Deletes one of the contact's own notes. The note must belong to the contact in the path: a note on another contact, on a deal or on an account is a 404 here. Only the user who wrote the note, or an admin user, may delete it. Returns 404 when the contact does not exist, the note is not one of its notes, or the API user may not edit contacts; and 403 when the API user is neither the author nor an admin user, or the delete fails. The response body is an empty object.

contactId.description: ID of the contact the note belongs to

noteId.description: ID of the note to delete

actions.name: update_note_on_contact
actions.description: Update a note on a contact. Changes one of the contact's own notes. PATCH on this path does the same. The note must belong to the contact in the path: a note on another contact, on a deal or on an account is a 404 here. Only the user who wrote the note may change it. Fields left out of the body keep their values, and mdate is set to now. When is_draft goes from 1 to 0, the draft is published and the contact note webhook fires for every list. Returns 404 when the contact does not exist, the note is not one of its notes, or the API user may not edit contacts; 403 when the API user did not write the note; and 422 when the note text is set to blank.

contactId.description: ID of the contact the note belongs to

noteId.description: ID of the note to update

note.description: The changes to make. Every member is optional. A body that is not a JSON object, or a note member that is not an object, is treated as an empty note: only mdate changes.
The new text of the note. Emoji are removed, HTML characters are escaped and surrounding spaces are trimmed before it is saved. 422 when it is blank or null.

is_draft.description: 0 or 1. 1 keeps the note as a draft. Setting 0 on a draft publishes it, and the contact note webhook fires.

mentionStrings.description: Usernames to mention, each written as @username. Every matching user who is not already mentioned on this note gets a mention record and a notification. Existing mentions are kept. Not returned on the note.

actions.name: remove_contact_tag_by_name
actions.description: Remove a tag from a contact by tag name. Removes one tag from a contact, addressed by contact id and tag name, without needing the contactTag association id that DELETE /contactTags/{id} requires. Pass the tag name in the tag query parameter. To remove by tag id instead, use DELETE /contacts/{contactId}/tags/{tagId}; exactly one of the two must be used per request. The tag definition itself is not deleted. Returns 404 if the contact does not exist, the tag name does not exist, or the tag is not applied to that contact. Names containing commas or line breaks fail with 400.

tag.description: Name of the tag to remove from the contact.

actions.name: apply_contact_tags
actions.description: Apply tags to a contact. Applies up to 100 tags to one contact in a single request, by tag name, tag id, or both. Tag names that do not exist yet are created automatically unless createMissing is false; tag ids must refer to existing tags. This replaces the per-tag sequence of GET /tags, POST /tags, and POST /contactTags with one call. Returns 201 with every requested association, including ones that already existed, so the request is safe to repeat. Send at least one entry in tags or tagIds. Tag names are matched case-insensitively, and are trimmed and stripped of HTML markup before matching and creation. Returns 404 if the contact does not exist. Fails with 400 for an unknown tag id, an...

tags.description: Tag names to apply. A name that does not exist yet is created, unless createMissing is false. Emoji and other 4-byte characters are not supported.

tagIds.description: Ids of existing tags to apply, as positive integers or numeric strings. An unknown id fails the request with 400.

createMissing.description: Whether to create tags for names that do not exist yet. Only applies to tags; unknown tagIds always fail. Set it to false to apply existing tags only.

actions.name: remove_contact_tag_by_id
actions.description: Remove a tag from a contact by tag id. Removes one tag from a contact, addressed by contact id and tag id, without needing the contactTag association id that DELETE /contactTags/{id} requires. To remove by tag name instead, use DELETE /contacts/{contactId}/tags with the tag query parameter. The tag definition itself is not deleted. Returns 404 if the contact does not exist, the tag does not exist, or the tag is not applied to that contact. A tag id that is not a positive integer, or a request that also passes the tag query parameter, fails with 400.

tagId.description: ID of the tag to remove from the contact

actions.name: find_contact
actions.description: Retrieve a contact. Retrieve an existing contact. The response embeds, as top-level arrays beside contact, the contact's contactLists (each with its channel), contactData, fieldValues, geoIps with their geoAddresses, deals (with exclude[]=deals the contact's deals are not loaded and deals comes back as an empty array), accountContacts with their accounts when the Accounts feature is enabled, and contactAutomations only when automations=true. The embedded arrays are fixed. For other relationships use the sub-resource reads, for example GET /contacts/{id}/contactTags.

id.description: ID of the contact

automations.description: Set to true to also embed the contact's contactAutomations. They are left out otherwise.

exclude[].description: Set to deals (exclude[]=deals) so the contact's deals are not loaded; deals then comes back as an empty array. Only the array form is read; exclude=deals does nothing.

actions.name: update_contact
actions.description: Update a contact. Update an existing contact. Fields you leave out keep their current values. Custom field values in contact.fieldValues are saved in the same request; fields you leave out are not changed. The user needs the edit contacts permission. PATCH on this path behaves exactly like PUT: both methods run the same action, with the same body and responses. If your account uses social channels, custom fields whose service is engage are kept up to date automatically by those channels: values sent for them are ignored, and the other fields still save.

id.description: ID of the contact to update

contact.description: The contact fields that create and update both accept. On update, only the fields you send change.

email.description: The contact's email address. Line breaks are removed, and so are spaces at either end. It must be valid and no other contact may have it, or the request fails with 422. Required on create, unless allowNullEmail applies. On update, leave it out to keep the current address.

phone.description: The contact's phone number. Must be a string; a number fails with 422.

allowNullEmail.description: Set to true to save the contact without an email address. This only works when the account has phone-only contacts turned on. The phone must then be unique, and is required unless the contact has a channel identity. When phone-only contacts are off, an email is still required. Leave email out or send null; an empty string still fails.

fieldValues.description: Custom field values to save with the contact. Each item sets one field. Fields you leave out are not changed. The saved values are returned in the top-level fieldValues array of the response.

field.description: Id of the custom field.

value.description: The new value. Lists are only supported for checkbox and listbox fields. For those fields, a string with the options separated by || also works.

fields.description: Deprecated: use fieldValues. The old name for fieldValues, with the same items. Ignored when fieldValues is sent.

items.description: A field and value, as in fieldValues.

field.description: Id of the custom field.

value.description: Value to store in the custom field, validated against the type of the field.

account.description: Links the contact to an account. Send either id or name, not both. Needs the Accounts feature and the edit contacts permission, or the request fails with 403. When sent, organization and account_name are ignored.

id.description: Id of an existing account. An id that does not exist fails with 422.

name.description: Name of the account. Spaces at either end and letter case do not matter. If no account has this name, the request fails with 422 unless createIfMissing is true.

createIfMissing.description: Only with name. Set to true to create the account when no account has the name. Creating needs the add accounts permission, or the request fails with 403. Defaults to false. The account is created before the contact is checked, so it stays even if the request then fails.

organization.description: Deprecated: use account. Id of the account to link the contact to. Ignored when account is sent.

account_name.description: Name of the account to link the contact to. The contact links to the account with this name, which is created if none has it. Used only when neither account nor organization is sent, and only when the account has the Accounts feature; otherwise ignored. The account is created before the contact is checked, so it stays even if the request then fails.

orgid.description: Deprecated: use account. Id of the account to link the contact to. If sent together with account or organization, orgid wins.

tags.description: Names of tags to add to the contact. A name that no tag has yet creates that tag. Tags the contact already has stay, and so do tags you leave out; this field never removes a tag. In each name, commas and line breaks become spaces, and HTML, emoji and spaces at either end are removed. A name that is then empty or longer than 250 characters fails with 422. New tags are created before the contact is checked, so they stay even if the request then fails.

lists.description: Lists to subscribe the contact to. Each list you name becomes an active subscription, also when the contact was unconfirmed or unsubscribed on it. The exception is a double opt-in form in contact.form; see form. Lists you leave out are not changed. A non-empty list needs the edit contacts permission, on create too, or the request fails with 403. All lists are checked before the contact is saved, and the contact is not saved if one fails. A list that does not exist, or an item with a key not listed here, fails with 422. So does resubscribing a contact who unsubscribed from the list, unless the user has the permission to resubscribe contacts. An email list needs a contact with an email address and an SMS list needs one with a phone number, or the request fails with 400. The mail options below do nothing while a subscription is unconfirmed.

sdate.description: When the subscription started, as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS or YYYY-MM-DD (start of that day). It is set even when the contact is already on the list. Leave it out to keep the current date; a new subscription, or one that becomes active again, then starts now. Any other format fails with 422.

sendInstantAutoresponder.description: Set to true to send the list's subscribe autoresponders even when the contact was already on the list or had unsubscribed. Cannot be true together with suppressInstantAutoresponder. Accepts true, false, 1, 0 and the strings true, false, yes, no, on, off, 1 and 0, in any letter case. An empty string counts as false. Other values fail with 422.

suppressInstantAutoresponder.description: Set to true to not send the list's subscribe autoresponders. Accepts true, false, 1, 0 and the strings true, false, yes, no, on, off, 1 and 0, in any letter case. An empty string counts as false. Other values fail with 422.

sendLastCampaign.description: Set to true to send the contact the last campaign sent to the list, even when the list is not set up to do that. Accepts true, false, 1, 0 and the strings true, false, yes, no, on, off, 1 and 0, in any letter case. An empty string counts as false. Other values fail with 422.

form.description: Id of a form. The write then acts like a submission of that form. The contact is also subscribed to the form's lists, with the same permission and checks as lists. If the form uses double opt-in, every list subscription this request creates stays unconfirmed, including lists named in contact.lists. The confirmation email is sent when one of the form's own lists gets a new subscription, and the form's actions and its submit automations run once the contact confirms. Otherwise they run now. An id that is not a form fails with 422.

ip4.description: The IPv4 address the contact signed up from. It is saved on the contact, where ip in the response shows it as a number, and on the list subscriptions this request creates. An address that is not IPv4, such as an IPv6 address, fails with 422. An empty string or null records nothing.

whatsapp_id.description: The contact's WhatsApp user id from Meta. Used only when the account has a WhatsApp inbox; otherwise it is dropped, and so is whatsapp_username when sent with it. It also needs phone-only contacts turned on, or the request fails with 422. With a whatsapp_id the email address is optional. If another contact already has this id, the request fails with 409.

whatsapp_username.description: The contact's WhatsApp username. Without a WhatsApp inbox it is dropped when sent with whatsapp_id, and saved when sent alone.

channelIdentities.description: Identities of this contact on connected messaging channels. Used only on accounts where channel identity contacts are enabled; ignored otherwise. The same source, channelAccountId and externalId may not appear twice in one request.

source.description: Messaging channel the identity belongs to: instagram or messenger.

channelAccountId.description: ID of the connected channel account the identity belongs to. At most 64 characters.

externalId.description: ID of the person on that channel. At most 255 characters.

open_tracking_optout.description: 1 when the contact has opted out of open pixel tracking, 0 when not. On PUT, sending 0 for a contact that has never answered (open_tracking_optout_updated_at is null) records the current time as its consent date; leave the field out to keep the contact unanswered.

useDefaults.description: Accepted for compatibility with the custom field value endpoints; it has no effect when saving a contact.

actions.name: delete_contact
actions.description: Delete a contact. Deletes one contact. The contact is removed from all of its lists and its tags are removed, and its email address is anonymized in the unsubscribe log and other related records. Its account link and its secondary-contact deal links are deleted. Each deal on which it is the primary contact moves to the deal's first secondary contact; a deal with no secondary contact but an account stays on that account with no contact; any other such deal is deleted, with its tasks. A copy of the contact record is kept in the contact archive for 360 days, where it can be restored once it is old enough; Admin users can see archived contacts with GET /contactArchives. The user needs permiss...

id.description: The contact id

actions.name: get_contact_account_contacts
actions.description: Retrieve a contacts account contacts. The link between this contact and its account (company): the account id, the contact's job title there, and when the link was created and last changed. A contact can be on one account at a time, so the list normally holds at most one row and is empty when the contact has no account. Everything comes back in one response: limit, offset, filters and orders are ignored on this path. To find links across contacts, use GET /accountContacts with filters[contact] or filters[account]. Returns 404 if the contact does not exist.

id.description: ID of the contact

actions.name: get_contact_automation_entry_counts
actions.description: Retrieve a contacts automation entry counts. For each automation this contact has entered, the number of times they entered it. Hidden automations (the ones the app creates to add form submitters to a list) are left out. Rows are ordered by automation id. Everything comes back in one response with no links or meta: limit and offset are ignored. Only GET is allowed. Returns 404 if the contact does not exist.

id.description: ID of the contact

actions.name: get_contact_bounce_logs
actions.description: Retrieve a contact's bounce logs. The bounce log entries recorded for this contact, one per bounced message with its timestamp, bounce code and campaign. For every bounce log on the account, use GET /bounceLogs. Neither endpoint filters by a date range, so a bounce count for a period is not available in one request. Every entry comes back in one response: limit and offset are ignored on this path.

id.description: ID of the contact

actions.name: get_contact_automations
actions.description: List all automations the contact is in. The automation runs this contact has been in, one entry per time the contact entered an automation. status 1 means the contact is still moving through the automation; 2 means the run has ended. adddate is when the contact entered and remdate when the run ended. By default every run comes back in one response. Pass limit to page; offset then applies and defaults to 0. Without limit, offset is ignored. orders[lastdate]=ASC or DESC sorts by the last activity in the run; any other direction is rejected with 422. Returns 404 if the contact does not exist. To list runs across contacts, use GET /contactAutomations. The contactAutomations link on a contact ...

id.description: ID of the contact to receive automations for

orders[lastdate].description: Order the rows by lastdate, the most recent time something happened to the contact in that automation. Use asc or desc in any letter case (asc, ASC, desc, DESC, Desc are all accepted; the value is upper-cased before it is checked); any other value is rejected with a 422 error. Without it the order is not guaranteed.

actions.name: get_contact_data
actions.description: Retrieve a contact's data. The contact's data record: one row of extra information the application keeps about the contact, mostly where the contact appears to be located. The location fields (geoIp4, geoCountry2, geo_country, geoState, geoCity, geoZip, geoLat, geoLon, geoTz, geoTzOffset, geoTstamp) are filled by a MaxMind GeoIP lookup of an IP address recorded for the contact, for example when the contact subscribes, opens or clicks a tracked email, or is added through the v1 API with an ip4 value; contact enrichment can also fill the city, state, country, country code and zip when they are blank, and sets geoTstamp when it does. The ga_campaign_*, ga_first_visit, ga_times_visited, fb_id...

id.description: ID of the contact

actions.name: get_contact_deal_associations
actions.description: Retrieve a list of contact's deals. The deals this contact is on as a secondary contact, as contact-to-deal links. Each link carries the deal id (deal), the contact id (contact), the contact's role on the deal (role, null when none) and when the link was made (cdate). Deals where this contact is the primary contact are not listed here; GET /contacts/{id}/deals returns those. Every link comes back in one response: limit and offset are ignored on this path, and no order is guaranteed. The linked deals are sideloaded in deals and their primary contacts in contacts. A user without the permission to list all deals sees only links to deals they own. Returns 404 if the contact does not exist. Fo...

id.description: ID of the contact

actions.name: get_contact_data_goals
actions.description: Retrieve a contact's goals. The automation goals this contact has reached, one entry per goal reached in one automation run. goal is the goal id, automation the automation id, and contactAutomation the id of the run (an entry of GET /contacts/{id}/contactAutomations). Every entry comes back in one response: limit and offset are ignored on this path. Returns 404 if the contact does not exist.

id.description: ID of the contact

actions.name: get_contact_lists
actions.description: Retrieve a contact's list memberships. The lists this contact is on, one row per subscription with its status and dates. To answer how and when a contact left a list: status 2 is unsubscribed and 3 is bounced; udate is when the membership was unsubscribed or bounced and is null while it is active (a resubscribe clears it and resets sdate); unsubreason is the reason recorded with an unsubscribe, empty when none was given; sourceid says how the subscription was created (0 unknown, 1 import, 2 sync, 3 account user, 4 API, 5 form, 6 form opt-in, 7 trigger, 8 SMS, 9 automation, 10 bulk edit, 11 email, 12 Gmail). Every membership comes back in one response: limit and offset are ignored on this ...

id.description: ID of the contact

actions.name: get_contact_logs
actions.description: Retrieve a contact's logs. Log entries recorded against this contact. merge is the only action written today, recorded on the surviving contact, so most contacts have an empty list. Every entry comes back in one response: limit, offset, filters and orders are ignored on this path. Returns 404 if the contact does not exist.

id.description: ID of the contact

actions.name: get_contact_tags
actions.description: List the tags applied to a contact. List the tags applied to one contact, as contact-to-tag associations. Each item's tag is the tag id (fetch the name with GET /tags/{id}, or several at once with GET /tags?ids=1,2), and its id is the association id to pass to DELETE /contactTags/{id}. Returns every association the contact has: limit and offset are ignored. Associations whose tag has since been deleted are not shown. Returns 404 if the contact does not exist. GET /contactTags?filters[subscriberid]={id} returns the same associations with paging, plus any whose tag has been deleted. To apply tags use POST /contacts/{id}/tags; to remove one use DELETE /contacts/{id}/tags/{tagId}.

id.description: The contact id.

actions.name: get_contact_deals
actions.description: Retrieve a contact's deals. The deals on which this contact is the primary contact. Deals where the contact is only a secondary contact are not included; GET /contacts/{id}/contactDeals lists the contact's secondary-contact links. At most 100 deals come back and no order is guaranteed: limit, offset, filters and orders are ignored on this path, so a contact with more than 100 deals cannot be paged here. A user who is not allowed to see all deals gets only the deals they own. A deal in a pipeline the user cannot see comes back with isDisabled true and only its id, title and status. To find deals across contacts, use GET /deals, which supports filters such as filters[status], filters[stage]...

id.description: ID of the contact

actions.name: get_contact_field_values
actions.description: Retrieve a contact's field values. Returns every stored custom field value of one contact. The whole set is always returned: limit and offset are ignored on this endpoint. Each entry's field property is the custom field definition id; entries exist only for fields the contact has a stored value for, and for lookup fields. A lookup field shows a field of the contact's account and stores no value of its own: its entry is never saved, its id has the form lookup-{contactId}-{fieldId}, and it carries lookupFieldType, the type of the field shown (e.g. currency, date, datetime, multiselect), and fieldCurrency, the currency code of a currency value, for the value to be read as that type; a curren...

id.description: ID of the contact

actions.name: get_contact_geo_ips_list
actions.description: Retrieve a contacts list of geo-ips. The IP addresses recorded for this contact, with the campaign and message they were seen on. Each entry carries the address as a number in text form (ip4) and the id of the location it resolved to (geoAddress); links.geoAddress leads to that location. At most 100 entries are returned, in no guaranteed order; limit and offset are ignored on this path. Returns 404 if the contact does not exist.

id.description: ID of the contact

actions.name: get_contact_organization
actions.description: Retrieve a contacts organization. The account (company) this contact belongs to, in the older organization shape: name, owner and dates. The account is found from the account id stored on the contact or, when that is not set, from the contact's account link. The response is an empty object {} when the contact has no account. This read is kept for compatibility; prefer GET /contacts/{id}/accountContacts and then GET /accounts/{id}, which also returns the account's website. Returns 404 if the contact does not exist.

id.description: ID of the contact

actions.name: get_contact_plus_append
actions.description: Retrieve a contacts plus append. Social profile details that contact enrichment has attached to this contact: a photo URL and Facebook, Twitter and LinkedIn profile URLs. This path serves a reduced copy of the record, so only those fields come back here; the last_updated dates and the other enrichment columns are not included. A contact has at most one such record, so limit and offset do not apply. The response is an empty object {} when the contact has none. Returns 404 if the contact does not exist.

id.description: ID of the contact

actions.name: get_contact_score_values
actions.description: Retrieve a contact's score value. The contact's current point totals: one row per contact score, plus one row per deal for each deal score (deal is then that deal's id). score is the id of the score definition (see GET /scores), scoreValue is the points the contact holds for it, and deal is null for contact scores. Rows for scores that have since been deleted are left out. Every row comes back in one response and no order is guaranteed: limit, offset, filters and orders are ignored on this path. Returns 404 if the contact does not exist.

id.description: id of the Contact

actions.name: get_contact_tracking_logs
actions.description: Retrieve a contacts tracking logs. Returns every site-tracking and event-tracking log entry recorded for a contact. Each entry's id is the eventId that GET /trackingLogs/{eventId}/contact accepts; entry ids come from their own account-wide sequence and are unrelated to contact ids. The full list is returned in one response; limit and offset are ignored on this route (use GET /trackingLogs with filters[subscriberid] for a paginated listing). An entry's type is __pagevisit for a site-tracking page visit (value holds the page URL), __redir for a tracked link redirect (value holds the destination URL), or the name of an event-tracking event (value holds the event data). Entries are copied int...

id.description: The contact's id (as returned by GET /contacts)

actions.name: search_content_manager_files
actions.description: Search the Content Manager for files. Files stored in the account's Content Manager, found by title, keyword or alt text, one page at a time: 20 files by default and 40 at most, with fileCount giving how many match in all. Results are not only images: filter with mimeType or mimeTypes to keep one kind of file, or check each file's mimeType. Pass folderId to search one folder. Use sort=added,desc for newest first. Each file carries its storage key, and its address is built from baseUrl and that key together.

name.description: Search text. Matches part of a file's title, one of its keywords or its alt text.

folderId.description: Only files directly in this folder.

mimeType.description: Only files of exactly this type, such as image/png. Matching is exact: image/* matches nothing.

mimeTypes.description: Only files of any of these types, separated by commas, such as image/jpeg,image/png,image/gif. Matching is exact.

size.description: How many files per page, from 1 to 40. A larger value is rejected with a 400.

sort.description: Order as property,direction: the property is name, size or added, the direction asc or desc. Any other property is ignored. Use added,desc for newest first. Without it the order is not defined.

actions.name: get_content_manager_file
actions.description: Retrieve a Content Manager file. One file from the account's Content Manager by its ID: its title, alt text, type, size, dimensions, keywords and storage keys, and who last changed it and when. Answers 404 when the account has no such file. Unlike the search and the lists, retrieving by ID can still return a file that was deleted.

id.description: ID of the file.

actions.name: get_folders_containing_file
actions.description: Show which folders a Content Manager file is in. Which custom folders of the Content Manager hold one file, given the file's ID.

id.description: ID of the file.

actions.name: list_keywords_on_content_manager_file
actions.description: List the keywords on a Content Manager file. The keywords added to one file in the Content Manager. These are the words the search matches on besides the file's title.

id.description: ID of the file.

actions.name: list_content_manager_folders
actions.description: List all Content Manager folders. Every custom folder in the account's Content Manager, with its ID and name. Deleting a folder leaves its files in the Content Manager.

actions.name: get_content_manager_folder
actions.description: Retrieve a Content Manager folder. One custom folder from the account's Content Manager by its ID.

id.description: ID of the folder.

actions.name: list_files_in_content_manager_folder
actions.description: List the files in a Content Manager folder. The files in one custom folder of the account's Content Manager. The API does not page this list and limit and offset do nothing here: the catalog cuts the response at 100 files and its truncation note gives the full count. For a larger folder use the file search with folderId and page. Each file carries its storage key, and its address is built from baseUrl and that key together.

id.description: ID of the folder.

actions.name: list_files_with_keyword
actions.description: List the files with a keyword. The files in the account's Content Manager that have one keyword. Find a keyword's ID from a file's keywords. The API does not page this list and limit and offset do nothing here: the catalog cuts the response at 100 files and its truncation note gives the full count. For a keyword with more files use the file search with name set to the keyword and page. Each file carries its storage key, and its address is built from baseUrl and that key together.

id.description: ID of the keyword.

actions.name: check_email_authentication_of_from_address_domain
actions.description: Check the email authentication of a From address domain. Builds the email-authentication notice the campaign designer shows for a campaign's From address. Only the first domain in domains is checked. For a free-mail domain (gmail.com, googlemail.com or yahoo.com) the notice is always a warning, filled in with a substitute sending address built from fromEmail (its local part and domain joined with a dot, at <account ID>.emcampaign.com) and with replyEmail. For any other domain Hosted checks the domain's DKIM, DMARC and DNS records: the notice describes the first problem found, and when none is found appearance is success and title and description are empty. Texts are translated into the us...

domains.description: Domain of the From address to check. A comma-separated list is accepted, but only the first domain is checked.

fromEmail.description: The campaign's From address. Only used for a free-mail domain, to build the substitute sending address the notice names.

replyEmail.description: The campaign's reply-to address. Only used for a free-mail domain, where the notice names it.

isAdmin.description: 1 when the user is an admin. Any other value gives the non-admin wording and a help article link.

actions.name: get_editor_markup
actions.description: Get Editor Markup. The HTML and CSS the campaign designer (Stripo) stores for one campaign message: the editable design, not the compiled email. Unlike GET /content/messageMarkup/{messageId}, the strings are returned as stored, apart from three conditional-content comment markers (`<!-- %IF`, `% -->` and `<!-- %/IF% -->`) that are restored when they were saved HTML-escaped. A message with no stored designer markup, including an ID that names no message, answers 404.

actions.name: list_conversions
actions.description: List conversions.

search.description: Filters by conversion name, case-insensitive substring match.

with_counts.description: When 1, adds lifetime total/last-triggered counts to each conversion.

is_required_by_goal.description: When 1, adds is_required_by_goal and folder_ids to each conversion.

limit.description: Number of conversions to return per request. Defaults to 20; the maximum is 100, and asking for more is capped at 100.

offset.description: Number of conversions to skip before returning results. Use with limit to page.

actions.name: create_conversion
actions.description: Create a conversion.

name.description: Plain text only -- HTML tags are stripped server-side.

value.description: Dollar value of a single conversion event. Stored as cents internally; this is the dollar amount.

limit.description: Max times a single contact may trigger this conversion. Only enforced when enforcelimit is 1.

value_option.description: 0 = no value, non-zero = has a dollar value option. Exact enum not fully confirmed.

field_data.description: Personalization-tag reference for a dynamic conversion value, format 'x::tagname'.

actions.name: list_conversion_statistics
actions.description: List conversion statistics. Read-optimized conversion stats (counts, values, graph series), separate from GET /conversions. Backed by ConversionsService::fetchConversionData().

ids.description: Comma-separated conversion IDs. Omit to return all conversions (paginated by limit/offset).

initiativeId.description: Scopes backfill/goal/overlay data to this business goal. Required for include_backfill and include_graph_overlay to take effect.

use_overview_config.description: When 1, uses the account's saved Overview sort-order configuration instead of ids.

actions.name: create_conversion_label
actions.description: Create a conversion label.

actions.description: List conversion labels. A 'conversion label' (ConversionFolder) is the association row between a conversion and a label/folder -- not the label itself.

actions.description: Bulk-create conversion labels.

actions.name: bulk_delete_conversion_labels
actions.description: Bulk-delete conversion labels.

actions.name: set_conversion_target_for_business_goal
actions.description: Set a conversion's target for a business goal.

actions.description: Retrieve a conversion label.

include_conversions.description: 1 adds the conversion's id, name, value and currency to the label (conversionId, conversionName, conversionValue, conversionCurrency).

actions.name: update_conversion_label
actions.description: Update a conversion label. The conversion and label association is immutable after creation -- only goalType, goalValue, and conversionTargetStatus may be updated. Attempting to change conversion or label returns 400.

actions.name: delete_conversion_label
actions.description: Delete a conversion label.

fieldType.description: Type of field. Possible values are: `text`, `textarea`, `date`, `datetime`, `dropdown`, `multiselect`, `radio`, `checkbox`, `hidden`, `currency`, `number`, or `lookup`. A `lookup` field shows a field of a related object instead of holding a value of its own, and is configured through `field_options`. The type of an existing field is never changed by an update, so a field has to be created as a `lookup`.

fieldOptions.description: Options for the field. A list of values, necessary if `field_type` is `dropdown`, `multiselect`, `radio`, or `checkbox`. For a `lookup` field it is an object instead: `{"lookup": {"object": "account|contact|deal", "field": "<field id>"}}`, naming the object and the field whose value is shown. An update may change a lookup field's configuration, and an update that omits it keeps the stored one.

fieldDefault.description: Default value of the field. For a `date` field use YYYY-MM-DD; YYYY/MM/DD and MM/DD/YYYY are also accepted, and the value is stored as YYYY-MM-DD.

fieldDefaultCurrency.description: The 3-letter currency code of the default currency for the field. Only necessary if `field_type` is `currency`.

isFormVisible.description: Whether or not the field is visible on forms

isRequired.description: 1 to make the field required, 0 (the default) to leave it optional. A required field does not need a `fieldDefault`. Creating a deal through POST /api/3/deals or a deal CSV import needs a value for every required field, unless the field has a `fieldDefault`, which counts as one: POST /api/3/deals answers 422 with an error naming the field and its `customFieldId`, and a deal import skips the row and lists it in the import's errors. Automations, forms and API v1 `deal_add`, which can't send custom field values, do not enforce the setting and create the deal with the field empty, and updating an existing deal is never refused because a required field is empty. Hidden, lookup and calculated fields are never enforced.

sendoptin.description: Whether the form sends an opt-in confirmation email to contacts it subscribes to a list. The email is created with `POST /form/optin`, must contain `%CONFIRMLINK%`, and is only sent once its ID is saved in `optin_id`.

optin_id.description: ID of the campaign holding the form's opt-in confirmation email. Save it with `PUT /forms/{id}` after `POST /form/optin`, or the form won't send the email. Responses fill it in as a number once the campaign exists, whether or not it is saved, so don't take it there as proof that it is.

optin_created.description: Whether the opt-in confirmation email has been set up. Absent until the email is created. Responses work it out from the campaign, whatever is saved.

confaction.description: What happens after a contact clicks the link in the opt-in confirmation email: `show-message` shows the form in `confform`, and `redirect` opens `confurl`

confform.description: ID of the form that shows the confirmation message, used when `confaction` is `show-message`

confurl.description: Address opened after confirming, used when `confaction` is `redirect`

preferenceCenterType.description: The kind of preference center the form is. Only `open-tracking` exists: a preference center without lists that manages only the open tracking opt-out. It is set when the form is created, needs the open tracking preference center feature flag, and is kept as stored on every update: any value sent to `PUT /forms/{id}` is ignored. Missing on every other form.

paused.description: Whether the form is paused: it accepts no submissions and shows visitors a paused message in place of its fields. Missing when the form has never been paused. Only `PUT /forms/{id}/pause` and `PUT /forms/{id}/resume` change it; any value sent to `POST /forms` or `PUT /forms/{id}` is ignored.

paused_message.description: The message a paused form shows visitors. Missing or empty: a default message. Saving trims it, and returns `422` when it is too long.

paused_link_text.description: Text of the button a paused form shows under its message. Send it with `paused_link_url`: saving one without the other returns `422`.

paused_link_url.description: The web address the paused form's button opens. Saving adds the secure scheme to an address without one, and returns `422` for anything else that isn't a web address.

blocked_email_domains.description: Email domains the form refuses submissions from, lowercase and at most 100. `example.com` blocks addresses at example.com only; `*.example.com` blocks every subdomain of example.com but not example.com itself.

block_personal_email_providers.description: Whether the form refuses addresses from personal email providers, such as gmail.com and yahoo.com

sms_confirmation_message.description: The SMS that asks a contact to confirm

sms_doi_success_message.description: The SMS sent once a contact confirms

sms_doi_address_id.description: ID of the address the confirmation SMS is sent with
