phone_prefix.description: Country code the phone input starts with

sms_consent.description: Whether the phone input asks for SMS consent

position.description: Pop-up layouts only: where the form appears, such as `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right`

initial_effect.description: Pop-up layouts only: how the form appears, such as `fade`, `slide-in` or `none`

show_delay.description: Pop-up layouts only: when the form appears. `scroll` waits until the visitor has scrolled to `delay_position`.

delay_position.description: Pop-up layouts only: how far down the page, as a percentage, the visitor scrolls before the form appears, when `show_delay` is `scroll`

hide.description: Pop-up layouts only: when a visitor stops seeing the form. `always` keeps showing it, `once` shows it once, and `interaction` stops after they interact with it.

hide_days.description: Pop-up layouts only: how many days until a hidden form shows again. Not used when `hide` is `always`.

preferencesConfirmed.description: What contacts see after saving their preferences. A default text shows for an empty key.

useBgColor.description: Form builder setting: whether the form uses its background color. `GET /forms/{id}` answers `true` when none is stored.

useBgImage.description: Form builder setting: whether the form uses a background image. `GET /forms/{id}` answers `false` when none is stored.

cfields.description: The form's inputs and content, in display order. Stored whole: sending it replaces every element. `GET /forms/{id}` returns `{}` for a form with none, and that can be sent back as it is.

items.description: One element of the form, in display order: an input, a heading or a block of content. Keys other than these are kept as sent; the form builder stores more for some types.

type.description: What the element is. Among others: `email`, `emailidentifier`, `fullname`, `firstname`, `lastname`, `phone`, `header`, `html`, `image`, `listsubscriptions`, `subscriptionmessage`, and the input types of custom fields, such as `text`, `textarea` and `checkbox`. An input for a custom field can leave it out, with `id` saying which field.

id.description: What the input fills in: the ID of a custom field, or the name of a standard one, such as `email`

header.description: Label of the input, or the text of a `header` element

required.description: Whether a submission must fill in this input.

html.description: For `html` elements: the content. Unsafe HTML is filtered out by `POST /forms` and `PUT /forms/{id}`.

class.description: CSS class the form builder gives the element

required_options.description: For inputs with options: the options that must be chosen, as an object keyed by option ID. With none it comes back as `[]` or `{}`, depending on how the form was saved.

parentformid.description: ID of the form this one is the opt-in confirmation page of. `0` on any other form.

addressid.description: ID of the address related to the form. `0` when it has none.

source.description: Where the form was made, at most 16 characters. Defaults to `builder`.

aid.description: `PUT /forms/{id}` only: ID of the address to set on the form's opt-in email campaign. Not stored on the form.

actions.name: list_forms
actions.description:
List all forms. Lists the account's forms with their settings, inputs and actions, by name A to Z unless `sort` says otherwise. Opt-in confirmation pages are left out.

Each form's `public_url` is its public link and `embed_code` is the snippet that places it on a website. `url` is the form builder's preview website, not the public link.

Requires the permission to edit forms.

limit.description: Number of forms to return. Defaults to 20, and values above 100 are reduced to 100.

offset.description: Number of forms to skip, for paging.

ids.description: Return only these forms. One id, or several separated by commas. Supersedes `limit`, which becomes the number of ids given.

search.description: Return only forms whose name contains this text.

layout[].description: Return only forms with these layouts, sent as `layout[]=<layout>` once per layout. A single `layout=<layout>` works too.

label.description: Return only forms in this folder (form label), by its id. `-1` returns forms in no folder; `0` returns every form, as leaving it out does.

filter.description: Return only forms with an action of this type.

branding.description: `true` lists only forms that show the ActiveCampaign branding badge (`style.ac_branding`), `false` only forms that don't, including forms that never set it. `1`/`0`, `yes`/`no` and `on`/`off` work too. Left out or empty: every form. Any other value returns `422`.

paused.description: `true` lists only paused forms, `false` only forms that aren't paused, including forms that were never paused. Matches the stored `options.paused`. `1`/`0`, `yes`/`no` and `on`/`off` work too. Left out or empty: every form. Any other value returns `422`.

sort.description: Order of the forms, by name A to Z when left out or not one of these: `name` or `nameD` by name, `layout` or `layoutD` by layout, `entries` or `entriesD` by number of submissions, `cdateA` or `cdateD` by created date. The values ending in D sort descending. Forms that tie are ordered newest id first.

include_folder.description: `1` adds each form's folders (form labels) to it as `labelsData`. Any other value leaves them out.

actions.name: get_form
actions.description:
Retrieve a form. Retrieves a form's settings, inputs and actions.

`public_url` is the form's public link and `embed_code` is the snippet that places it on a website. `url` is the form builder's preview website, not the public link.

Requires the permission to edit forms.

id.description: ID of the form to retrieve

actions.name: update_form
actions.description:
Update a form. Saves changes to a form. Keys left out keep their stored value.

`actiondata`, `submitdata`, `style`, `options` and `cfields` are each stored whole, so sending part of one removes the rest of it. To change one setting, read the form with `GET /forms/{id}`, change the setting and send that whole object back. `options.paused` is the exception: it keeps its stored value whatever is sent, and only `PUT /forms/{id}/pause` and `PUT /forms/{id}/resume` change it. `options.preferenceCenterType` keeps its stored value too: a form's type is set when it is created. On an `ipad` form, sending `options.sendoptin` as `true` keeps the stored options and ignores the rest of what is sent.

...

layout.description: How the form is shown. Layouts other than `inline-form`, `ipad` and `chat` need a plan with modal forms, and `preference-center` needs a plan with Preference Centers. Send it on every request: `POST /forms` can refuse a form without one, and `PUT /forms/{id}` without one keeps the stored layout but adds `fields` to `options`.

height.description: Floating bar layout: height of the form, in pixels

image.description: Older pop-up forms: address of the form's image. Newer forms use an `image` element in `cfields`.

options.description: The form's settings. Every key is optional, and keys other than these are kept as sent. The object is stored whole: an update that sends `options` replaces all of them, except `paused` and `preferenceCenterType`, which keep their stored values.

blanks_overwrite.description: Whether a blank input in a submission overwrites what is stored on the contact. When `false`, blank inputs are ignored.

sendoptin.description: Whether the form sends an opt-in confirmation email to contacts it subscribes to a list. The email is created with `POST /form/optin`, must contain `%CONFIRMLINK%`, and is only sent once its ID is saved in `optin_id`.

optin_id.description: ID of the campaign holding the form's opt-in confirmation email. Save it with `PUT /forms/{id}` after `POST /form/optin`, or the form won't send the email. Responses fill it in as a number once the campaign exists, whether or not it is saved, so don't take it there as proof that it is.

optin_created.description: Whether the opt-in confirmation email has been set up. Absent until the email is created. Responses work it out from the campaign, whatever is saved.

confaction.description: What happens after a contact clicks the link in the opt-in confirmation email: `show-message` shows the form in `confform`, and `redirect` opens `confurl`

confform.description: ID of the form that shows the confirmation message, used when `confaction` is `show-message`

confurl.description: Address opened after confirming, used when `confaction` is `redirect`

preferenceCenterType.description: The kind of preference center the form is. Only `open-tracking` exists: a preference center without lists that manages only the open tracking opt-out. It is set when the form is created, needs the open tracking preference center feature flag, and is kept as stored on every update: any value sent to `PUT /forms/{id}` is ignored. Missing on every other form.

paused.description: Whether the form is paused: it accepts no submissions and shows visitors a paused message in place of its fields. Missing when the form has never been paused. Only `PUT /forms/{id}/pause` and `PUT /forms/{id}/resume` change it; any value sent to `POST /forms` or `PUT /forms/{id}` is ignored.

paused_message.description: The message a paused form shows visitors. Missing or empty: a default message. Saving trims it, and returns `422` when it is too long.

paused_link_text.description: Text of the button a paused form shows under its message. Send it with `paused_link_url`: saving one without the other returns `422`.

paused_link_url.description: The web address the paused form's button opens. Saving adds the secure scheme to an address without one, and returns `422` for anything else that isn't a web address.

blocked_email_domains.description: Email domains the form refuses submissions from, lowercase and at most 100. `example.com` blocks addresses at example.com only; `*.example.com` blocks every subdomain of example.com but not example.com itself.

block_personal_email_providers.description: Whether the form refuses addresses from personal email providers, such as gmail.com and yahoo.com

sms_doi_enabled.description: Whether a form that subscribes contacts to an SMS list asks them to confirm by SMS

sms_confirmation_message.description: The SMS that asks a contact to confirm

sms_doi_success_message.description: The SMS sent once a contact confirms

sms_doi_address_id.description: ID of the address the confirmation SMS is sent with

fields.description: Which inputs an older pop-up form shows. Keys other than these are kept as sent.

name.description: Whether the form asks for a name

email.description: Whether the form asks for an email address

email_required.description: Whether the email address is required

phone.description: Whether the form asks for a phone number

phone_required.description: Whether the phone number is required

phone_validation.description: Whether the phone number is validated

phone_prefix.description: Country code the phone input starts with

sms_consent.description: Whether the phone input asks for SMS consent

position.description: Pop-up layouts only: where the form appears, such as `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right`

initial_effect.description: Pop-up layouts only: how the form appears, such as `fade`, `slide-in` or `none`

show_delay.description: Pop-up layouts only: when the form appears. `scroll` waits until the visitor has scrolled to `delay_position`.

delay_position.description: Pop-up layouts only: how far down the page, as a percentage, the visitor scrolls before the form appears, when `show_delay` is `scroll`

hide.description: Pop-up layouts only: when a visitor stops seeing the form. `always` keeps showing it, `once` shows it once, and `interaction` stops after they interact with it.

hide_days.description: Pop-up layouts only: how many days until a hidden form shows again. Not used when `hide` is `always`.

preferencesConfirmed.description: What contacts see after saving their preferences. A default text shows for an empty key.

useBgColor.description: Form builder setting: whether the form uses its background color. `GET /forms/{id}` answers `true` when none is stored.

useBgImage.description: Form builder setting: whether the form uses a background image. `GET /forms/{id}` answers `false` when none is stored.

cfields.description: The form's inputs and content, in display order. Stored whole: sending it replaces every element. `GET /forms/{id}` returns `{}` for a form with none, and that can be sent back as it is.

items.description: One element of the form, in display order: an input, a heading or a block of content. Keys other than these are kept as sent; the form builder stores more for some types.

type.description: What the element is. Among others: `email`, `emailidentifier`, `fullname`, `firstname`, `lastname`, `phone`, `header`, `html`, `image`, `listsubscriptions`, `subscriptionmessage`, and the input types of custom fields, such as `text`, `textarea` and `checkbox`. An input for a custom field can leave it out, with `id` saying which field.

id.description: What the input fills in: the ID of a custom field, or the name of a standard one, such as `email`

header.description: Label of the input, or the text of a `header` element

required.description: Whether a submission must fill in this input.

html.description: For `html` elements: the content. Unsafe HTML is filtered out by `POST /forms` and `PUT /forms/{id}`.

class.description: CSS class the form builder gives the element

required_options.description: For inputs with options: the options that must be chosen, as an object keyed by option ID. With none it comes back as `[]` or `{}`, depending on how the form was saved.

parentformid.description: ID of the form this one is the opt-in confirmation page of. `0` on any other form.

addressid.description: ID of the address related to the form. `0` when it has none.

source.description: Where the form was made, at most 16 characters. Defaults to `builder`.

aid.description: `PUT /forms/{id}` only: ID of the address to set on the form's opt-in email campaign. Not stored on the form.

actions.name: delete_form
actions.description:
Delete a form. Deletes a form, along with its opt-in confirmation page, its submission records and its folder links. This can't be undone.

Its opt-in email is deleted too when the user may delete campaigns; otherwise that campaign stays. The contacts the form collected stay in the account. To stop a form taking submissions without deleting it, use `PUT /forms/{id}/pause`.

Requires the permission to edit forms.

id.description: ID of the form to delete

actions.name: allow_personal_email_addresses_on_form
actions.description: Allow personal email addresses on a form. Makes the form take submissions from personal email providers, such as gmail.com, again, by setting `options.block_personal_email_providers` to `false`. Domains on `options.blocked_email_domains` stay blocked, gmail.com included if it is listed there. Allowing when they are already allowed changes nothing and succeeds. Use `PUT /forms/{id}/blockPersonalEmailProviders` to block them again. Requires the permission to edit forms.

id.description: ID of the form

body.description: The JSON ActiveCampaign takes for this call, as its API docs show it. Leave out when the call needs nothing more than its ids.

actions.name: block_personal_email_addresses_on_form
actions.description: Block personal email addresses on a form. Makes the form refuse submissions from personal email providers, such as gmail.com, yahoo.com and outlook.com, by setting `options.block_personal_email_providers` to `true`. The providers come from a list ActiveCampaign keeps, so they need not be added to `options.blocked_email_domains` one by one; the domains on that list stay blocked as before. Blocking when they are already blocked changes nothing and succeeds. Use `PUT /forms/{id}/allowPersonalEmailProviders` to take them again. Preference Center forms take no typed email address, so this has no effect on one. Requires the permission to edit forms.

id.description: ID of the form

body.description: The JSON ActiveCampaign takes for this call, as its API docs show it. Leave out when the call needs nothing more than its ids.

actions.name: block_email_domains_on_form
actions.description: Block email domains on a form. Adds email domains to the form's `options.blocked_email_domains`, so the form refuses submissions from addresses at them. Each domain is trimmed and lowercased, and a leading `@` or `*@` is dropped, as `PUT /forms/{id}` does: `@Competitor.com` is stored as `competitor.com`. `example.com` blocks addresses at example.com only; `*.example.com` blocks every subdomain of example.com but not example.com itself, so add both to block both. Domains already on the list are left as they are, so the request is safe to repeat. A form blocks at most 100 domains. Use `DELETE /forms/{id}/blockedEmailDomains` to unblock one, and `PUT /forms/{id}/blockPersonalEmailProviders` ...

id.description: ID of the form

domains.description: Domains to block, at least one, such as example.com or *.example.com. One invalid entry fails the request and nothing is added.

actions.name: unblock_email_domain_on_form
actions.description: Unblock an email domain on a form. Removes one domain from the form's `options.blocked_email_domains`, so the form takes submissions from addresses at it again. Pass the domain in the `domain` query parameter. It is cleaned as it was when added, so `@Competitor.com` removes `competitor.com`. Removing `*.example.com` leaves `example.com` blocked if it is on the list, and the other way round. To unblock personal providers such as gmail.com, use `PUT /forms/{id}/allowPersonalEmailProviders`. Requires the permission to edit forms.

id.description: ID of the form

domain.description: The blocked domain to remove, such as competitor.com or *.example.com

actions.name: get_form_html
actions.description: Retrieve a form's HTML. Returns the HTML that embeds the form on a page, rendered by the server, as text/html rather than JSON. While the form is paused, the body is what the form's script embed shows instead: the paused message for an inline form whose owner set a message or button of their own, otherwise an empty body. Requires the permission to edit forms.

id.description: ID of the form

actions.name: pause_form
actions.description:
Pause a form. Stops a form taking submissions, without deleting it. Its ID, settings and embed code stay the same.

While it is paused, visitors see a message in place of its fields: `options.paused_message`, or a default message when that is empty. When `options.paused_link_text` and `options.paused_link_url` are both set, the message has a button. Set those options with `PUT /forms/{id}`.

The form's public link always shows the message. An inline form's embed shows it only when the form has its own message or button, and renders nothing otherwise. The embeds of pop-up layouts render nothing.

Pausing a paused form changes nothing and succeeds. A Preference Center can't be paused, becau...

id.description: ID of the form to pause

body.description: The JSON ActiveCampaign takes for this call, as its API docs show it. Leave out when the call needs nothing more than its ids.

actions.name: resume_paused_form
actions.description: Resume a paused form. Resumes a paused form: it accepts submissions again, and its public link and embeds show its fields. Only `options.paused` changes, to `false`; the paused message and button stay saved for the next pause. Resuming a form that isn't paused changes nothing and succeeds. Use `PUT /forms/{id}/pause` to pause it again. Requires the permission to edit forms.

id.description: ID of the form to resume

body.description: The JSON ActiveCampaign takes for this call, as its API docs show it. Leave out when the call needs nothing more than its ids.

actions.name: list_geographical_addresses
actions.description: List all geo addresses. Lists the locations that contact IP addresses have resolved to across the account. Normally one location is stored per pair of coordinates and is shared by every address and contact that resolves there. There are no filters and no sort options; locations come in no guaranteed order. Use limit and offset to page, or ids to fetch specific locations.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of location ids to return. Overrides limit; offset still applies.

limit.description: The number of records to return for each call. Default is 20; maximum value is 100.

offset.description: Offset index of records to return.

actions.name: get_geographical_address
actions.description: Retrieve a geo address. Returns one location. Returns 404 if no location has the id.

id.description: ID of the location.

actions.name: list_geographical_ip_entries
actions.description: List all geo IP entries. Lists the IP addresses recorded for contacts across the account. An entry is recorded when a contact does something from an IPv4 address that resolves to a location, for example when the contact opens or clicks a campaign, submits a form, or is added through the v1 API with an IP address. The same contact, campaign and location is recorded once. The entries' locations are included in a top-level `geoAddresses` array. There are no filters and no sort options; entries come in no guaranteed order. Use limit and offset to page, or ids to fetch specific entries.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of geo IP entry ids to return. Overrides limit; offset still applies.

limit.description: The number of records to return for each call. Default is 20; maximum value is 100.

offset.description: Offset index of records to return.

actions.name: get_geographical_ip_entry
actions.description: Retrieve a geo IP entry. Returns one geo IP entry with its location in a top-level `geoAddresses` array. The array is absent when the entry has no location. Returns 404 if no geo IP entry has the id.

id.description: ID of the geo IP entry.

actions.name: get_ip_entry_location
actions.description: Retrieve the location of a geo IP entry. Returns the location that one geo IP entry resolved to. The id is the id of the geo IP entry, not of a contact or a location. Returns an empty object `{}` when the entry has no location, for example when the location record was removed. Returns 404 if no geo IP entry has the id.

id.description: ID of the geo IP entry.

actions.name: create_import_bulk
actions.description: Bulk import contacts. Import up to 250 contacts in one request. Asynchronous: the response returns a batchId and a successful response only means the import was accepted, not finished — poll GET /import/info with the batchId to confirm it completed before relying on the results. Contacts are matched by email (or by email_hash): existing contacts are updated and new ones are created, so an import is safe when some of the contacts already exist. Lists and tags are set per contact: use each contact's subscribe array to add it to lists, and its tags array to tag it (tags that do not exist are created). There is no request-level list id; one sent outside a contact is ignored. Contacts added to...

content_type.description: The body is read as JSON whatever this header says.

api_token.description: Your API key. Its user needs the contact import permission.

contacts.description: The contacts to import: at least 1 and at most 250 per request. A request with more than 250 is rejected with 400 and nothing is queued. Each contact needs an email, or an email_hash of an existing contact, or a phone when enable_contacts_without_email is true. For fewer than about 10 contacts, POST /contact/sync per contact is simpler.

items.description: One contact. Must have email, or email_hash, or phone together with the request-level enable_contacts_without_email option.

email.description: The contact's email address. Used to find an existing contact to update; otherwise a new contact is created. Must be a valid address. Required unless email_hash is given, or phone is given and enable_contacts_without_email is true.

email_hash.description: The hash of an existing contact, as returned in the hash field of GET /contacts. Use it instead of email to update a contact whose email you do not have, or do not want to change; the stored email is kept. A contact must have email or email_hash (or phone with enable_contacts_without_email).

phone.description: The contact's phone number, as a string. With enable_contacts_without_email set to true, a contact may be identified by phone alone.

customer_acct_name.description: The name of the account (organization) to link the contact to. Created if it does not exist, and the contact is linked to it.

tags.description: Tag names to apply to the contact. Tags that do not exist yet are created. Tag names cannot contain commas.

fields.description: Custom field values to set on the contact. Each entry needs the custom field's numeric id and a value. Field ids come from GET /fields. A non-integer id or a missing value fails validation for the whole request (400).

id.description: The ID of the custom field. Custom fields must be referenced by the ID that ActiveCampaign assigns to them. You can retrieve the ID number for a custom field by using the "List all custom fields" API call.

value.description: The value to store. For multi-value fields, separate values with the double-pipe delimiter, for example ||foo||bar||. Values for dropdown, list box, radio and checkbox fields that do not match an existing option are added as new options unless exclude_new_field_options is true.

subscribe.description: Lists to add the contact to, one object per list. This is the only way to put imported contacts on a list; a list id outside a contact is ignored. The contact is added with status active. A list that does not exist is skipped quietly. If the contact is already on the list as unconfirmed, previously bounced, previously unsubscribed, or is on the exclusion list, the row is recorded as a partial success (codes 104 bounced, 116 unsubscribed or unconfirmed, 130 exclusion list) and, for bounced, unsubscribed and excluded contacts, every subscribe entry on that contact is skipped. The contact is still created or updated. GET /import/info counts these rows as success; a callback with detailed_results counts them as failures.

listid.description: The id of the list. Find list ids with GET /lists.

unsubscribe.description: Lists to remove the contact from, one object per list.

listid.description: The id of the list. Find list ids with GET /lists.

ip.description: The IPv4 address to record as the contact's subscribe and last-seen IP. Optional.

job_title.description: The contact's job title on its account (organization). Only applied on accounts with the accounts feature. Optional.

open_tracking_optout.description: Whether the contact has opted out of open pixel tracking. Accepts 1/0, true/false or yes/no. Optional.

exclude_automations.description: Set to true so the import does not start automations for the imported contacts. Must be a JSON boolean; any other type is rejected with 422.

send_webhooks.description: Set to false to suppress webhooks for the imported contacts. When omitted, contact, custom field and tag webhooks are sent but list subscription webhooks are not; set to true to send list webhooks as well. Must be a JSON boolean; any other type is rejected with 422.

enable_contacts_without_email.description: Set to true to allow contacts that have a phone number but no email. Each such contact is identified by its phone. Must be a JSON boolean; any other type is rejected with 422.

exclude_new_field_options.description: Set to true so custom field values that do not match an existing option of a dropdown, list box, radio or checkbox field are not added as new options.

delete_after.description: A date and time after which the import's per-contact status records may be removed. Any format PHP's strtotime understands, for example 2026-12-31 or +30 days. An unparseable value is rejected with 422.

callback.description: Optional. A request the importer makes to your endpoint when the import finishes. This is the only way to receive per-row failure reasons for an API import.

url.description: The URL the importer calls once the import has completed.

requestType.description: GET or POST. Required. Any other value fails validation (400).

detailed_results.description: Include this key (any value, for example "true") to have the callback body carry the results: success and failures counts, an always-present failure_reasons array (empty), and, only when there were failures, a failure_results array with the email, code and message of every row that was not fully imported. Rows that imported but had a list subscription skipped (codes 104, 116, 130) are counted as failures here even though GET /import/info lists them as success. Only meaningful with requestType POST. Presence is what turns it on; the value itself is ignored.

params.description: A list of parameters to include in the callback request. Add each parameter in the form of a key-value pair. For a GET request, each parameter will be appended to the end of the URL in a query string. For a POST request, parameters will be included in the body of the request.

key.description: Name of the parameter. Required: an entry without key fails validation.

value.description: Value of the parameter. Required: an entry without value fails validation.

headers.description: A list of headers to include in the callback request. Add each header in the form of a key-value pair.

key.description: Name of the header. Required: an entry without key fails validation.

value.description: Value of the header. Required: an entry without value fails validation.

actions.name: list_bulk_import_status_aggregate
actions.description: Summarize recent API bulk imports by day. Summarize this account's API bulk imports from the last 7 days: for each day, how many batches and contacts are still outstanding and how many completed. Only imports submitted through POST /import/bulk_import are counted; imports started from the app's import tool or by integrations never appear here (use GET /import/history for those). There is no per-batch or per-contact detail and no error information, so this cannot explain why an import failed; for one batch use GET /import/info with its batchId. Both arrays are empty when nothing was imported through the API in the last 7 days. A batch that stalled and has a failed chunk is left out of outs...

actions.name: list_import_history
actions.description: List contact imports made from the app or by integrations. List this account's contact imports that were started from the app's import tool (CSV or file uploads) or by an integration, newest first, with how many rows imported, partly imported, or failed. Use it to answer questions about an import a user ran in the app, then use GET /import/history/{importId}/{type} to get the rows that failed and why. Imports submitted through POST /import/bulk_import do not appear here; check those with GET /import/info. Users outside the main user group only see imports from their own group. Paginated with limit (1 to 100, default 20) and offset; meta.total is the number of imports visible to the caller...

limit.description: Number of imports to return. Defaults to 20; the maximum is 100. Values outside 1 to 100 are rejected with 422.

offset.description: Number of imports to skip. Use with limit to page through the history.

actions.name: list_import_failures
actions.description: List the rows of an app or integration import that failed or were only partly imported, with reasons. For one import from GET /import/history, list the rows that did not import (type failure) or that imported but had a list subscription skipped (type partial), each with its email and the reason. This is the endpoint to use when a user asks why their import had errors. It covers imports started from the app or by an integration only; imports submitted through POST /import/bulk_import are not in the history and their reasons are only available through the import callback. Returns at most 500 rows, oldest first, and there is no paging beyond that. For partial rows the reason starts with "Imp...

importId.description: The import id, from the id field of GET /import/history.

type.description: failure for rows that were not imported; partial for rows that were imported but had a list subscription skipped. Contacts on the exclusion list appear under failure for imports run by the older import path and under partial for current ones, so check both when looking for excluded contacts. Anything else is a 422.

actions.name: get_bulk_import_status_info
actions.description: Bulk import status info. Check the status of one API bulk import using the batchId returned by POST /import/bulk_import. If the import has not finished yet, wait and poll again rather than resubmitting the same contacts. success lists the ids of the contacts that were created or updated; failure lists the email of each row that was not imported, with no reason. Optional flags add each goal's association counts and linked conversions. Query parameter names are accepted in camelCase or snake_case (`isArchived` or `is_archived`).

limit.description: Number of business goals per page, 1 to 100.

actions.name: list_notes
actions.description: Retrieve list of all notes. Lists notes. A note belongs to one record: a contact, a deal, a deal task, a contact activity entry or an account, named by reltype and relid. Only notes the caller is allowed to see are returned. Notes on activity entries are always shown. Notes on contacts need permission to edit contacts (pg_subscriber_edit), notes on deals need deal access (pg_deal) and an account with Deals, notes on deal tasks need permission to see all deals (pg_deal_list_all), and notes on accounts need permission to edit accounts (pg_account_edit). Drafts are left out unless filters[is_draft] asks for them. Without orders, the order of the notes is not defined. There is no error respon...

filters[reltype].description: Only notes on this kind of record. Exact match.

filters[relid].description: Only notes on the record with this id. Send filters[reltype] too, because ids of different kinds of record overlap.

filters[contact_id].description: Only notes on this contact. The same as filters[reltype]=Subscriber with filters[relid], and replaces both. When more than one of filters[account_id], filters[contact_id] and filters[deal_id] is sent, only the first in that order is used.

filters[deal_id].description: Only notes on this deal. Works like filters[contact_id], with reltype Deal.

filters[account_id].description: Only notes on this account. Works like filters[contact_id], with reltype CustomerAccount.

filters[include_related].description: Send with filters[account_id] to also return the notes on the account's contacts and deals, newest first. Sending the parameter at all switches to this mode, but the contact and deal notes are only added when its value is not empty or 0. In this mode drafts are included, and filters[is_draft], filters[reltype], filters[relid], filters[cdate] and orders are ignored; ids no longer picks notes but still caps how many are returned. Known defect: with filters[contact_id] or filters[deal_id] instead, it returns notes on any contact, deal or account whose id equals the given id.

filters[is_draft].description: 0 for published notes, the default, or 1 for drafts. Send it twice as filters[is_draft][]=0&filters[is_draft][]=1 to get both.

filters[cdate].description: Only notes created at exactly this date and time, written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. Comparison operators are not supported.

orders[cdate].description: Sort by creation time: DESC for newest first; any other value sorts oldest first. orders[reltype] and orders[relid] sort the same way by those fields.

limit.description: Number of notes to return. Defaults to 20; values above 100 are treated as 100. 0 or a negative number returns every note and ignores offset.

offset.description: Number of notes to skip. Use with limit to page through the notes.

ids.description: Comma-separated note IDs to return. When set, only those notes are returned; limit does not apply, but offset still does.

include_contact.description: Contact ids separated by | (pipe). Only notes on those contacts (reltype Subscriber) are returned; sent together with include_deal or include_account, notes on any of the named records are returned. Drafts stay excluded unless filters[is_draft] asks for them, and limit and offset still page the result.

include_deal.description: Deal ids separated by | (pipe). Only notes on those deals (reltype Deal) are returned: the way to read the notes of several deals in one call. Combines with include_contact and include_account the same way.

include_account.description: Account ids separated by | (pipe). Only notes on those accounts (reltype CustomerAccount) are returned. Combines with include_contact and include_deal the same way.

actions.description: Update a note. Update an existing note on a contact, deal, task, activity, or account. Categories the account is not entitled to (deals, accounts, ecommerce, custom objects) are omitted. `categories` maps each category code to its display label, returned as a translation key.

The catalog is not paginated: `limit` and `offset` are ignored and the response has no `meta`.

Ecommerce and custom object tags are read from the account's custom object schemas. If that read fails, any request that includes `ECOMMERCE` or `CUSTOM_OBJECT` ...

actions.name: update_account_settings
actions.description:
Update account settings. Update the settings of the user the API key belongs to, and the account wide date and time formats. This is the v3 replacement for the v1 `settings_edit` action, which wrote nothing but those formats.

The settings of the calling user (`firstName`, `lastName`, `loginEmail`, `timezone`, `language`) are required in every request: this endpoint writes the settings the request carries, so submit the values from [`GET /settings/account`](https://developers.activecampaign.com/reference/retrieve-account-information) for the fields that should keep their value. The three formats are optional, and only an administrator may change them.

A successful request is a `202` repo...

firstName.description: The first name of the calling user. Required, and may not contain quotes.

lastName.description: The last name of the calling user. Required, and may not contain double quotes.

loginEmail.description: The email address the calling user signs in with, returned as `email` by `GET /settings/account`. Required, and has to be an address whose domain can receive email. Changing it to an address on an unverified domain sends a verification email and leaves the settings unchanged, reported as a `422`; changing it is not allowed at all when the account signs in through SSO. When it changes, the user's other sessions are signed out.

notificationEmail.description: The address ActiveCampaign sends the calling user's notifications to. Optional, and has to be an address whose domain can receive email.

phoneNumber.description: The phone number of the calling user, returned as `phone`. Optional, and has to be a valid number in international format; a bare national number is a `422`.

signature.description: The email signature of the calling user, which may contain HTML. Optional.

timezone.description: The timezone of the calling user. Required, and has to be a supported timezone.

language.description: The language the UI is shown in. Required, and has to be a full language name (e.g. `english`, `deutsch`) — not an ISO code like `en`.

currentPassword.description: The calling user's current password, required only when `newPassword` is submitted.

newPassword.description: A new password for the calling user. Optional; when it is submitted it has to differ from the current password and satisfy the account's password policy.

dateFormat.description: The account wide date format, returned as `date_format`, as a `strftime` pattern. This is v1 `settings_edit`'s `dateformat`. Optional, and only an administrator may change it; an empty format, or one with no `strftime` conversion such as `%m`, is a `422`.

timeFormat.description: The account wide time format, returned as `time_format`, as a `strftime` pattern. This is v1 `settings_edit`'s `timeformat`. Optional, administrator only.

dateTimeFormat.description: The account wide combined date and time format, returned as `date_time_format`, as a `strftime` pattern. This is v1 `settings_edit`'s `datetimeformat`. Optional, administrator only.

actions.name: check_dkim_records_of_domain
actions.description:
Check the DKIM records of a domain. Looks up the DKIM DNS records of a sending domain and reports whether email from it can be DKIM signed.

The check looks first for both ActiveCampaign CNAME records (`acdkim1._domainkey` and `acdkim2._domainkey`), then for the legacy `dk` TXT record, then for a DKIM TXT record at the account's own selector. Only a user in the Admin group may call it; any other caller is refused with a `422`, not a `403`.

Legacy endpoint: the file has no method guard, but the controller answers GET only and any other method is a `405`.

actions.name: add_domain_to_white_list
actions.description:
Add a site tracking domain. Add a domain to the site tracking whitelist by name. Site tracking must be enabled first (`PUT /api/3/siteTracking`) - adding a domain while it is disabled returns `403`.

A name may begin with `*` to whitelist subdomains (for example `*.example.com`), and must otherwise match `/^\*?[a-zA-Z0-9-.]*[a-zA-Z0-9]$/`: no scheme, no port, no path. Supply the bare domain, not a URL.

The response echoes the submitted object with `201`. This is the v3 equivalent of the API v2 `tracking/whitelist` action, which took a `domain` parameter and answered `{"domain": ..., "success": 1}`; v3 reports the outcome with the status code instead of a `success` flag. Use `POST /api/3/...

Remove a site tracking domain. Remove a domain from the site tracking whitelist by name. The path segment is the domain itself, as the list shows it and not URL-encoded - no lookup step is needed, unlike `DELETE /api/3/prism/urlWhitelistings/{domainId}`, which requires the whitelisting id.

Site tracking must be enabled; the request returns `403` while it is disabled, even for a domain that is on the whitelist. A domain that is not whitelisted returns `404` (API v2 `tracking/whitelist/remove` answered `200` with `success: 0`).

Reading or updating a single domain is not supported: `GET` and `PUT` on this path return `405` with `Allow: DELETE`.

actions.name: list_automation_sms_blocks
actions.description: List automation SMS blocks. Lists the SMS messages configured inside the account's automations (automation SMS blocks), 20 per request by default and at most 100; page with offset. Requires one of the SMS campaigns permissions (view, manage or send) when granular SMS permissions are enabled. `filters[name]` matches part of the name; operators are also accepted, e.g. `filters[name][starts_with]=Welcome` (`eq`, `neq`, `lt`, `lte`, `gt`, `gte`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `in`). Read only. This is the automation SMS block, not an SMS broadcast; broadcasts are served under `/sms/broadcasts`.

include.description: Comma-separated relationships to return alongside the blocks: `user`, `automation`, `address`.

start_date.description: Keeps the blocks with automated send activity on or after this day, `Y-m-d` in America/Chicago.

When it has not, one is suggested from the address on the account's brand form: the first available area code for its state and postal code, then for its state alone, then for its country. A brand form whose country is anything other than exactly `US` or `CA`, including none, gets an Illinois area code instead: 312, then 773, then any Illinois area code. Takes no parameters. Requires the SMS registration permission.

Creates a quiet-hours window for the account. `start` and `stop` are required `HH:MM` or `HH:MM:SS` times in UTC (hour 0-23, minute 0-59) and may not be equal; a `stop` earlier than `start` is a window that wraps midnight. start.description: Window start in UTC, HH:MM or HH:MM:SS (hour 0-23, minute 0-59). Must differ from `stop`.

stop.description: Window end in UTC, HH:MM or HH:MM:SS (hour 0-23, minute 0-59). Must differ from `start`.

actions.name: list_all_tags2
actions.description: List all tags. Returns tag definitions, each with subscriber_count, the number of contacts the tag is applied to. Contact tags are returned by default; pass type=template for template tags. To find a tag by exact name, use filters[tag] or filters[search][eq]; both match the whole name, ignoring case. For a partial-name search, use search: it is a case-insensitive substring match, so it returns every similarly named tag alongside the one asked for. Identify the tag you want by comparing the tag field of each result, never by its position in the list. To apply a tag to a contact, pass the returned id to POST /contactTags. Unrecognized filter and order parameters are silently ignored. When t...

search.description: Filters tags by name. Partial matches are included (a contains match), within the selected type only. If both search and filters[search] are sent, search wins and filters[search] is ignored. The characters % and _ in the value act as SQL wildcards, and a value of 0 is ignored.

filters[tag].description: Filters by exact tag name. The simplest way to look up one tag by name. Names are unique within a type, so at most one tag matches.

exact_tag.description: Exact tag name; the same as filters[tag].

tags[].description: Array form, tags[]=a&tags[]=b: returns the tags whose name is exactly one of the values, within the selected type. A single tags=value without brackets is ignored.

type.description: Selects which tag type the response contains: contact (the default) or template. Any other value is treated as contact. Every response contains only one type of tag. Sending filters[type] instead of this parameter does not work and can return an empty result.

filters[search][<operator>].description: Filters tags by name using the operator. Supported operators: eq (exact name match), neq, lt, lte, gt, gte, contains, starts_with. Send only one operator per request: when several are sent, the last value is applied to every operator. in is not supported here and returns an empty list, as does any other operator value.

filters[id][<operator>].description: Filters by tag id. Supported operators: eq, neq, lt, lte, gt, gte, and in with a comma-separated list of ids (for example filters[id][in]=1,2,3). Always send an operator: filters[id]=1 without one is a contains match on the digits, so it also returns ids such as 10 and 21.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of tag ids to return, or the array form ids[]=1&ids[]=2. Overrides limit. Only tags of the selected type are returned, so ids of template tags need type=template.

orders[search].description: Sorts search results by relevance: exact matches first, then tags starting with the searched text, then the rest. weight is the only supported value, and it only applies when filters[search] is also sent and the legacy order parameter is absent. Ordering by other fields is not supported; any other orders parameter is silently ignored and the default sort by id applies.

order.description: Legacy sort. popular orders by subscriber_count, highest first, and adds a count field to each tag (for type=template, count is the number of templates using the tag, reported as 1 for a tag no template uses); alpha orders by name, A to Z. Overrides the default id order and orders[search]=weight. Any other value leaves the list in no particular order.

direction.description: Sort direction for order. Defaults to desc for popular and asc for alpha; ignored without order.

selected_tag_id.description: Tag id, or array of ids, to place at the top of the list ahead of the normal ordering. Tags the filters exclude are not added.

template_in_use.description: When present with any value, returns only tags applied to at least one template. Meant for type=template.

include_automation_status.description: 1 adds has_automation to every tag in the response: true when a visible automation has a tag added or tag removed trigger for the tag, an add or remove tag action naming it, or a segment condition on the tag in its start or actions. It runs several extra queries per tag, so use a small limit.

include.description: Comma-separated related collections to add to the response: contactGoalTags, templateTags. Unknown names are ignored. GET /tags/{id} ignores this parameter.

limit.description: Number of results to return. Default 20. Values above 100 are capped to 100; the literal value null raises the cap to 1000 for that request.

offset.description: Number of results to skip. Use with limit to page through results.

actions.name: create_a_tag2
actions.description: Create a tag. Creates a tag definition. This does not apply the tag to any contact; to do that, pass the new tag id to POST /contactTags, or use POST /contacts/{id}/tags to create and apply by name in one call. Always send tagType (contact or template): a tag created without it does not appear in GET /tags listings. If a non-deleted tag with the same name and type already exists, the request returns 200 with the existing tag instead of creating a duplicate. If the name is held by a deleted tag that has not been purged, the request fails with 422 and a {message, error} body rather than an errors array. Tag names must be 1 to 250 characters and cannot contain commas, line breaks, or HTML ma...

tag.description: The tag name: 1 to 250 characters, no commas, line breaks, or HTML markup. Emoji and other 4-byte characters are not supported. Stored exactly as sent.

tagType.description: Type of the new tag: contact or template. Always send this; a tag created without a type does not appear in tag listings.

actions.name: get_tag
actions.description: Retrieve a tag. Returns a single tag definition, including subscriber_count, the number of contacts the tag is applied to. Use GET /tags with filters[tag] to find a tag by name when the id is not known. Unlike GET /tags, it also returns soft-deleted tags, with deleted set to 1, and template tags. Returns 404 only when no tag with this id exists. Query parameters, including include, are ignored.

id.description: ID of the tag to retrieve

actions.name: update_a_tag
actions.description: Update a tag. Updates a tag's name, type, or description. Renaming a tag also updates automations and segments that reference the old name. The new name follows the same rules as POST /tags: 1 to 250 characters, no commas, line breaks, or HTML markup, and emoji and other 4-byte characters are not supported; a name that breaks a rule fails with 422 (see the 422 response for the two body shapes). If another tag already uses the new name, the request fails with 422 and errors[0].detail is "Tag already exists". Returns 404 if the tag does not exist (unless the new name is already in use, which is checked first and returns 422). Requires the tag management permission.

id.description: ID of the tag to update

tag.description: The new tag name: 1 to 250 characters, no commas, line breaks, or HTML markup. Must not be in use by another tag.

tagType.description: Tag-type of the tag being updated. Possible Values: template, contact

description.description: Description of the tag being updated

actions.name: delete_tag
actions.description: Delete a tag. Deletes a tag definition. The delete is permanent: the tag no longer appears in GET /tags and GET /tags/{id} returns 404. The tag's associations to contacts are not deleted with it: they no longer appear under GET /contacts/{id}/contactTags, but GET /contactTags still lists them (for example with filters[tagid]) and counts them in meta.total, and each one can still be fetched with GET /contactTags/{id} and removed with DELETE /contactTags/{id}. Links from templates to the tag are removed. Automations and segments that reference the tag are not changed. To take a tag off a single contact without deleting the tag, use DELETE /contacts/{id}/tags/{tagId} instead. Returns 200 wit...

actions.name: create_email_template
actions.description:
Create a template. Create an email template. This is the v3 equivalent of the v1 `message_template_add` action.

Requires the `CreateEmailTemplates` permission. The new template is made available to the lists the authenticated user can access; users in the admin group create account-wide templates.

name.description: Template's name.

subject.description: Default subject line applied to campaigns built from this template.

userid.description: Owner of the template. Defaults to the authenticated user. Assigning another user requires permission to share templates with that user, otherwise the request answers `403`.

ed_version.description: Designer version the template is built for: `1` legacy, `2` current designer, `3` new designer.

hidden.description: Set to `1` to hide the template from the template gallery.

additional_data.description: Free-form JSON metadata stored with the template.

basecampaignid.description: Id of a campaign whose content the template is created from.

basetemplateid.description: Id of an account template, or the hash of a stock template, to copy content from.

actions.name: list_email_templates
actions.description: List all templates. Retrieve the email templates in the account. Results are paginated and can be filtered; `meta.total` holds the total number of templates matching the request. Responses include each template's full HTML by default and are large as a result; pass `exclude=content,preview_content` whenever the body is not needed.

limit.description: The number of templates to return for each call. Maximum value is 100.

offset.description: Offset index of records to return.

filters[name].description: Filter by template name. Matches any template whose name contains this value.

filters[source].description: Filter by the source the template was created from.

filters[read_only].description: Filter by read-only templates. Use 1 for read-only templates, 0 for editable ones.

filters[mdate].description: Filter by the date the template was last modified (YYYY-MM-DD).

filters[hidden].description: Filter by hidden templates. Use 1 for hidden templates, 0 for visible ones.

filters[ed_version].description: Filter by the designer version the template was built with.

filters[has_content].description: Set to `true` to only return templates that have content.

filters[tagid].description: Filter to templates carrying the given tag id.

exclude.description: Comma-separated list of response fields to omit. Use `exclude=content,preview_content` unless the caller needs the template's HTML body: those two fields carry the whole email and dominate the response. On a five-template account the full response is roughly 512 KB, of which about 123 KB per record is `content` and about 60 KB is `preview_content`; omitting both returns the same ids, names, URLs and timestamps in roughly 2.6 KB. Listing, searching, counting and identifying templates need none of the omitted fields. Not supported on `GET /templates/{id}`, which always returns the full record.

actions.name: get_template
actions.description: Retrieve a template.

actions.name: update_email_template
actions.description:
Update a template. Update an existing email template. This is the v3 equivalent of the v1 `message_template_edit` action.

Requires the `UpdateEmailTemplates` permission and access to the template being updated, otherwise the request answers `403`; an unknown id answers `404`.

The content of the template can also be reseeded from an existing campaign or template instead of being supplied directly: send `basecampaignid` to copy the content of a campaign message, or `basetemplateid` to copy the content of another template (a numeric id, which requires access to that template) or of a stock template (its identifier). The design of the source is carried over with the markup.

id.description: ID of the template to update

name.description: Template's name.

hidden.description: Set to `1` to hide the template from the template gallery.

basecampaignid.description: Reseed the content of this template from the message of the given campaign. Mutually exclusive with `basetemplateid`.

basetemplateid.description: Reseed the content of this template from another template. A numeric id copies that template; any other value is treated as a stock template identifier. Mutually exclusive with `basecampaignid`.

actions.name: list_tracked_events_and_their_contacts
actions.description: List the tracked events that have fired, with their contacts. Lists site-tracking and event-tracking log entries across all contacts, 20 per page by default. Each entry's id is the eventId that GET /trackingLogs/{eventId}/contact accepts. Use filters[subscriberid] to scope the list to one contact. Use only the query parameters documented here: unsupported filter and order fields are silently ignored, so the response looks filtered but is not. An entry's type is __pagevisit for a site-tracking page visit (value holds the page URL), __redir for a tracked link redirect (value holds the destination URL), or the name of an event-tracking event (value holds the event data). Entries are copied i...

filters[subscriberid].description: Return only entries belonging to this contact id. Exact match.

filters[tstamp].description: Return only entries recorded at this exact date and time, formatted YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS in the account's timezone. A date without a time matches only entries recorded at exactly 00:00:00.

filters[type].description: Return only entries whose type contains this text (substring match). Operator suffixes such as filters[type][eq] are not supported on this endpoint and fall back to the same substring match.

orders[tstamp].description: Order entries by recorded time. ASC or DESC.

orders[subscriberid].description: Order entries by contact id. ASC or DESC.

orders[type].description: Order entries by type. ASC or DESC.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of entry ids to fetch. Overrides limit.

include.description: include=contact adds a contacts array to the response holding the contact each entry belongs to.

limit.description: Number of entries per page. Default 20, maximum 100.

offset.description: Number of entries to skip, for pagination.

actions.name: get_contact_by_event_id
actions.description: Get Contact By Event ID. Returns the contact that a tracking-log entry belongs to. eventId must be the id of a tracking log entry, as returned by GET /contacts/{id}/trackingLogs or GET /trackingLogs. It is not a contact id and not an event-tracking event name. Passing a contact id returns 404 (No Result found for TrackingLog) when no entry has that id, or the contact of an unrelated entry when one does, so a 200 does not mean the id spaces are interchangeable. To fetch a contact by contact id, use GET /contacts/{id} (get-contact) instead. To list the tracking events of a known contact, use GET /contacts/{id}/trackingLogs.

eventId.description: The id of a tracking log entry: the id field returned by GET /contacts/{id}/trackingLogs or GET /trackingLogs. Not a contact id and not an event name; to look up a contact by its id use GET /contacts/{id} instead.

actions.name: get_tracking_log_entry
actions.description: Retrieve a tracking log entry. Returns a single tracking log entry by its id. The same id is the eventId that GET /trackingLogs/{eventId}/contact accepts. Entry ids are returned by GET /trackingLogs and GET /contacts/{id}/trackingLogs; they are not contact ids. Returns 404 if no entry has the given id.

id.description: The tracking log entry's id. Not a contact id.

actions.name: create_user
actions.description: Create a user. Create a new user with full account access, gated by their group (role). All of `username`, `email`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `group` and `password` are required — there is no partial or invited-user creation. `password` must be at least 8 characters; `username` may contain only lower-case letters and/or numbers, no spaces.

username.description: Username. Lower-case letters and/or numbers only, no spaces.

password.description: Plain text password. At least 8 characters.

actions.name: list_users
actions.description: List all users. List all existing users of the account, paged with limit and offset. Narrow the list with search (part of a username, name or email), usernames, ids, groups or a filter on username, first name, last name, email or phone; every parameter is optional. The list is not narrowed by the caller's user group. Records are in the `users` key and `meta.total` counts every match.

limit.description: Number of users to return, at most 100. Defaults to 20.

offset.description: Number of users to skip. Defaults to 0.

ids.description: Comma-separated user ids to return; when sent, the page size is the number of ids given.

search.description: Keeps the users whose username, first name, last name, first and last name together (as in `Jane Doe`) or email contains this text. Partial text matches, and the characters % and _ match themselves. search=0 or an empty value applies no filter.

usernames.description: Comma-separated usernames; keeps the users whose username is exactly one of them.

filters[username].description: Keeps the users whose username contains this text.

filters[firstName].description: Keeps the users whose first name is exactly this. `filters[first_name]` is accepted as well.

filters[lastName].description: Keeps the users whose last name is exactly this. `filters[last_name]` is accepted as well.

filters[email].description: Keeps the users whose email is exactly this.

filters[phone].description: Keeps the users whose phone contains this text.

groups[].description: Keeps the users who belong to any of these user group ids; repeat it to send several.

deals.description: `owner` keeps the users who own a deal; `task_assignee` keeps the users who have a deal task assigned to them.

actions.name: create_single_sign_on_token_for_user
actions.description:
Create a single sign-on token for a user. Mint a short lived single sign-on token for a user, so an application can drop that user straight into the ActiveCampaign UI without asking them for their password. This is the v3 equivalent of the v1 `singlesignon` action, and the token it returns is produced by the same implementation.

The token is spent by sending the user to `https://{account}.activehosted.com/admin/main.php?_ssot={token}`, from the IP address the token was bound to. Spending a token does not consume it: it stays usable from that address until it expires.

Only a user in the **Admin** group may call this endpoint, and only for a user they may administer; anything else is a `4...

id.description: Id of the user to mint the token for

ipAddress.description: The IP address the token may be spent from. Pass the address of the browser the user will arrive from, or `__self` to bind the token to the address this request came from, which is then reported back in the response. A value that is neither a valid IP address nor `__self` is a `422`.

duration.description: How long the token remains valid, in minutes, between 1 and 1440. Defaults to 15 minutes when omitted.
